想.story: Post a lookout on top of your heart and let him report on things that aren't in front of him yet — that is thinking a thing up.
想.note: 相 is carrying the sound ソウ; the lookout is a memory-hook, not a real semantic contribution.

意.story: Whatever sound rises off a person's heart when they finally open their mouth is their meaning, the intention sitting under the words.

愛.story: A claw catches a heart, a crown is drawn over it to keep it, and the trailing foot cannot make itself step away — that is love.

感.story: A war cry goes up and the heart lurches before you have decided anything, and that involuntary lurch is feeling.

戦.story: One side loads the slingshot, the other lifts the dagger-axe, and the argument has officially become a war.

損.story: Fingers reach into the roster and pluck out a member, so the count comes up short, and short is a loss.
損.note: 員 is along for sound and shape, not meaning; the plucked member is a pure memory-hook.

携.story: Fingers clamped around a plump bird's legs, hauling it with you from village to village rather than leaving it behind.

数.story: The rice woman works under the whip, tallying grain after grain, and the numbers pile up faster than she can call them out.

新.story: The axe drops the standing tree and the exposed wood underneath is pale, wet and unweathered — brand new, riding 亲's シン.

暖.story: Sun on your back while a tug-of-war drags on across the field, both teams sweating through their shirts because the day has turned warm.
暖.note: 爰 is only the sound part; the tug-of-war is a hook and claims nothing about the meaning.

暗.story: The sun is gone and only sound tells you where anything is — dark.

業.story: Whiskers of carved ornament along a bell rack, propped on beams the zodiac sheep dragged in, and assembling all that hardware is somebody's whole business.

楽.story: Horns, eight white bells, all of it strung up in one tree that starts ringing on its own, and the evening turns into fun.

歳.story: Every time the zodiac dog comes round again you press one small footprint into the calendar, and stacked prints are your age in years.

殿.story: A corpse lies in state, retainers stand together along the walls, a war club guards the door: you are inside the lord's palace, so mind your manners.

滅.story: Water droplets pour over the smothered fire until not even smoke is left standing.

漢.story: A scarecrow keeps watch over fields fed by water droplets off the great river, and that riverland is Han country, whose characters Japan borrowed whole.
漢.note: 𦰩 supplies only the カン sound; the scarecrow is a memory-hook with no claim on the meaning.

盟.story: The dish goes around the circle under a bright sky and every man drinks from it, and by the last swallow the alliance is sworn.

督.story: Uncle's eye stays on you the entire shift; he never picks up a tool himself, he just supervises.
督.note: 叔 is here for sound only — the eye carries the meaning and the uncle is a memory-hook.

節.story: Bamboo lays down a hard joint before each new stretch of growth, and the kneeling diner marks every one of those notches with a meal — the year divided into seasons.

続.story: Sell one spool of thread and the buyer knots it onto the end of the last one, so the line never actually stops.
続.note: 売 rides along for the sound; the selling is a hook rather than the real sense.

義.story: Hoist the sheep horns up above your own ego and let the sacrifice outrank you: that is righteousness.

腹.story: A bellows shaped like a fat moon sits under your ribs, filling and emptying all day long, and it rides 复's フク.
腹.note: 复 gives only the sound フク; the bellows is a memory-hook, not the character's real semantic.

解.story: Work the cleaver in where the horn joins the cow and the whole animal comes apart along its own seams, which is exactly what untying a knot or a problem feels like.

触.story: The insect leads with its horn, tapping whatever is ahead before it commits a single leg — touch first, trust after.

試.story: Make your words perform the entire ceremony from memory, bow by bow, and the one place they stumble is what the test was for.

詩.story: Words kept in a temple, chanted on a schedule until they keep their own time, come out as a poem.

話.story: The tongue rolls the words over and over until they come out as a story someone will sit still for.

誉.story: Words lifted onto a candelabra so the whole hall can read them by their own light — public praise, which is honor.

豊.story: Beans heaped over the rim of the stand in ridges like a washboard, more than anyone at the table could finish.

賃.story: You entrust a month of work and cowrie shells come back across the table as wages, and half of them go straight out again as rent.

資.story: Cowrie shells set aside for whatever comes next instead of spent tonight: that untouched pile is your assets.

路.story: A foot passes each welcome mat in turn, and the worn strip linking one doorway to the next is the road.

較.story: Two cars nose to nose with their bumpers crossed like crossed legs, and you cannot stop measuring one against the other.
較.note: 交 is the sound コウ; the crossed legs are a hook and make no claim about meaning.

辞.story: One spicy sentence off the tongue on the way out the door, and the job is over.

農.story: The dragon drags a washboard across the field, leaving ridge after ridge of turned soil behind it, which is farming before anyone invented the tractor.

違.story: Set out down the road in tanned leather and your track comes out crooked against everyone else's: different, and probably wrong.

遠.story: The hem of a trailing gown drags along the road, gray with dust from somewhere nobody here has ever been.

鉄.story: Gold you would shrug off losing, because it is only iron — and iron is what they lay the rails with.

雇.story: A small bird turns up at your door every morning wanting work, so you put it on the payroll.
雇.note: 戸 supplies only the コ sound; the door is a memory-hook, not part of the meaning.

電.story: Rain overhead, and under it the sun bent into a fishhook and flung down at the ground: lightning, the raw current we later ran through wires.

預.story: Hand your yo-yo across the counter and the clerk's head dips as he writes the ticket, and there it sits on deposit until you come back for it.

僕.story: A standing person hauling brushwood from dawn to dusk is the manservant, and ボク is what a man calls himself when he is not putting on airs.
僕.note: 菐 is pure sound (ボク); the brushwood is a memory-hook.

境.story: Soil runs right up to the finish line and stops; cross that stripe and the ground belongs to somebody else.

増.story: Soil goes on in layers like the stacked tiers of a steamer pot, one more every day, and the mound keeps getting taller.

察.story: From under the roof you watch the whole festival without ever joining it, and you can read the crowd's mood from where you sit.

慢.story: A pounding heart that stretches itself out to twice its actual size, all swagger and no hurry.

慣.story: Thread the same day onto a coin string a hundred times over and the pounding heart stops noticing it altogether.

構.story: Timber stack notched into the tree trunk until the frame braces itself and stands unaided — the stance you build and then hold, on 冓's コウ.

様.story: Sheep horns hung in a tree and doubled in the pond beneath it: a household keeping up appearances so carefully that you attach 様 to its name.

歌.story: Jaw dropped in a yawn, the chant comes out riding the breath.

歴.story: Under the cliff, footprints run through the grove in row after row, one row per generation, and reading them off is history.

漏.story: Water droplets work through the one bad tile in a leaky roof and drip on the floor all night, which is how secrets get out too.

演.story: The zodiac tiger paces the stage while water droplets catch the footlights, and it will prowl the identical path again tomorrow night.
演.note: 寅 is the sound component only; the tiger is a memory-hook.

端.story: Stand a seedling upright and look at the very tip where the shoot breaks into open air, the outermost edge of the whole plant.

曇.story: A cloud slides in front of the sun and the whole afternoon goes flat gray.

橋.story: Somebody bent a tree into a high arch over the river so people could walk across it.

機.story: A tree frame strung up and clicking away like an abacus: the loom, and after it every machine, and every chance the shuttle throws you.
機.note: 幾 is here for its キ sound only; the abacus clicking is a memory hook, not a real semantic contribution.

積.story: Cut grain stalks heap higher all season — and so does the blame if the heap comes up short.
積.note: 責 supplies the セキ sound and nothing else; blame is a hook, not part of the meaning.

築.story: Bamboo strapped against tree, the clamp cranked down tight, and the frame is built.

興.story: Eight lifting hands heave the same beam skyward as one, and the crowd's interest rises right along with it.

薦.story: Hold out an armful of flowers to the horned beast: an offering made on someone else's behalf, which is exactly what a recommendation is.

薬.story: Flowers that do for a sick body what music does for a sick mood — medicine.

親.story: Someone is out by the standing tree at the edge of the yard, watching to see you come home, every single evening — your parent.
親.note: 亲 is purely the シン sound (the same element as in 新); the standing tree carries no meaning here, only the image.

輸.story: Roll the car onto the dugout canoe, because the cargo has to keep moving whatever happens to be carrying it.

録.story: Gold letters cut one below the next, steady as a dripping bucket, until the whole account stands on record.

頭.story: A bean balanced on the crown of a head — the round hard knob sitting on top of you.
頭.note: 頁 carries the whole meaning; 豆 is there for its トウ sound, so the bean is a hook rather than a part of the word's sense.

頼.story: Hand the bundle over and let somebody else's head take the weight of it — that is relying on a person.
頼.note: 束 is a sound element (ライ); the bundle is a hook — the character's older form was built differently.

館.story: A hall whose entire ground floor is food, laid out for every bureaucrat in the prefecture.

優.story: A standing person who can put on a mourner's grief the instant the scene calls for it: superior on stage, gentle off it.

績.story: At season's end they measure the thread you actually spun, and that length is your results — any shortfall is your blame.
績.note: 責 gives only the セキ sound; the blame reading is a hook that pairs this with 積.

翼.story: Feathers fanning out from both arms of a masked figure give you one wing and then its mirror image.
翼.note: 異 is the sound element (ヨク); the masked figure is a picture to hang the feathers on, not a meaning.

謙.story: He is holding two stalks where everyone else managed one, and his words insist it was nothing.
謙.note: 兼 is phonetic (ケン); the two stalks are a memory image, not a claim about modesty.

講.story: Words stacked in order like a timber stack, square layer on square layer, until the lecture stands up on its own.

曜.story: The sun swings past again as quick as a pheasant across the window, and there goes another day of the week.
曜.note: 翟 is pure sound (ヨウ); the pheasant is a hook, and the sun does all the semantic work.

翻.story: The feathers take their turn flipping belly-up in the gust — everything reversed, which is also what happens to a sentence when you translate it.

職.story: Ear cocked for the next order, chisel already in hand: that pairing is your occupation.

藤.story: Under the moon, flowers pour off the trellis in a long pale gusher — wisteria.

観.story: Stand as still as a stork in the shallows and just see: nothing gets past that patient, whole-scene view.

鎮.story: Set a block of gold down on the truth so nothing flutters or rises again — weight that quiets a thing by sitting on it.
鎮.note: 真 is the チン sound only; the truth-under-a-weight image is a hook, not the character's real logic.

難.story: The small bird ignores the scarecrow entirely, which makes clearing it out of the field genuinely difficult.
難.note: This character originally named a bird and was borrowed wholesale for the sound; neither part really means "hard," so the scene is a hook.

題.story: The sundial's shadow points dead at the head of the page, at the one line that names the topic.
題.note: 是 is purely the ダイ sound; the sundial is an image, and 頁 (head, top of the page) carries the sense.

額.story: A guest arrives and the head greets you forehead-first — a flat pale panel wide enough to write a sum across.
額.note: 客 contributes the ガク sound and no meaning; the guest is a hook.

顔.story: Give a head the fine markings of a handsome man and you get the part everyone actually looks at.

顕.story: Sunlit silk shows every thread it has; hold a head in that same hard light and nothing about it stays hidden.

類.story: A big head bent over spilled rice, thumbing the grains into little piles by type.
類.note: The 大 was originally 犬 (dog), and the sorting scene is a hook — this character's composition is not transparently meaningful.

験.story: The whole assembly turns out to watch the horse run, because running it is the only way to test what it is made of.
験.note: 㑒 is the sound element (ケン) shared with 検 and 険; the assembly is a hook, not a meaning.

識.story: Chisel the words into the marker post so that later you can tell this one from that one.

警.story: Respect walks in first and the words come fast behind it — that is a warning, and that is the police.

願.story: Head bowed at the edge of an open meadow, saying out loud the one thing you want.
願.note: 原 supplies the ガン sound; the meadow sets the scene but adds nothing to the meaning.

懸.story: Your heart is strung up beside the hanging head, left dangling there with everything you care about at stake.

競.story: Two contenders, shoulder to shoulder, neither one willing to give back a single step.

議.story: Weighing words the way you weigh out the cuts of a sacrificial ram — nobody leaves the council until the shares are right.

護.story: Steady words spoken over the bird while the birdcatcher's hands close around it — caught, and kept safe.

躍.story: The foot pushes off the way a pheasant explodes out of tall grass — straight up, all at once.
躍.note: 翟 is the ヤク sound element; the pheasant is a vivid hook, and the foot carries the meaning.

顧.story: The head you hire turns back over its shoulder to check on the work it just walked past.
顧.note: 雇 is here for its コ sound; hiring plays no part in the meaning.

発.story: Splayed feet planted on the two chalk marks, legs coiled — the whole character is the instant before departure.
発.note: The 二 and 儿 are leftovers of the older 弓+殳 (bow and weapon) that sat below the feet; read them as shape, not meaning.

皆.story: Compare one face to the next down the whole row and every single one shines back the same white — everyone, no exceptions.
皆.note: The 白 here descends from 自 (self/nose), not 'white'; the shining faces are a memory hook.

相.story: Bring an eye right up against a tree until each fills the other's entire view — looking and being looked at in the same instant, which is mutual.

省.story: The eye that reads a fat report and leaves only a few lines standing — the scrutiny that names a government ministry and the habit of cutting things out.

県.story: An eye hung from an L-bracket with small threads swinging beneath it — a head strung up at the boundary of each prefecture.
県.note: These parts are the wreckage of an upside-down 首 hung by a cord; treat them as shape rather than meaning.

研.story: Work the blade against the stone until the edge runs as level as a torii's crossbeam — grinding, polishing, and the long grind we call research.
研.note: 开 supplies only the sound ケン; the torii is a pure memory hook.

祝.story: Kneeling at the shrine, the older brother speaks the good words out loud over the family — celebrating.

神.story: Lightning splits the sky above the shrine and something up there announces itself — the god, riding 申's シン.

秋.story: Grain stalks gone the color of fire, stubble smoking at the edge of the field — autumn.

科.story: Scoop the grain stalks out with a dipper and sort them bin by bin — every measured pile becomes its own department.

約.story: A thread wound round a teacup and cinched by eye rather than measured — approximately, about this much, which is also the loose knot you tie when you promise.
約.note: 勺 is purely phonetic; the teacup carries no meaning of its own.

紅.story: Silk thread hauled dripping out of the dye vat and hung over a carpenter's square to dry — crimson.
紅.note: 工 contributes only the sound コウ.

級.story: Thread knotted at intervals, each knot the next rung you reach — notches that count off your rank.
級.note: 及 mainly carries the sound キュウ; the reaching is a hook.

美.story: Great sheep horns strapped high on a dancer's head, big enough to see from the back row — the old picture of beauty.

胃.story: Everything the rice paddy grows ends up churning down below the moon — the stomach.

背.story: Turn north, away from the sun, and all anyone gets from you is the moon on your back.

茶.story: A pedestrian stoops under the flowers of a sapling, stripping off the leaves that will become tea.

要.story: The west cap clamps over a woman's hips like two hands at the waist — the hinge the whole body turns on, so the one thing you cannot do without.
要.note: 覀 is not 'west' here but a pair of hands at the waist; use the cap shape only as a hook.

計.story: Words counted off ten at a time until the tally becomes a measurement and the measurement becomes a plan.

負.story: A beak hooked into a cowrie shell you now have to carry on your back — the debt, and the losing end of it.

追.story: Down the road after whatever just went over the earth mound ahead — the chase in which you only ever see its back.

退.story: The stubborn eye finally gives it up, turns, and takes the road back the way it came — retreat.

送.story: See the traveller off down the road with a lit torch held high — the same word for sending a letter, a parcel, or anything else on its way.

郎.story: Not one crumb of the family estate up on the city's hill has come to him yet — the young man, the -rō closing out every Tarō and Jirō.
郎.note: The left side is a squeezed 良 acting as sound, not a crumb; the crumb is a hook.

重.story: A bale lashed at the middle of a standing figure, the whole load pressing straight down through him — heavy, and heavier with every layer piled on.
重.note: No reliable decomposition — the modern shape is a worn-down drawing of a man bearing a bundle.

限.story: The hill looks back at you with a stubborn eye: this far and no farther — your limit.

面.story: Pull the hat brim down low until nothing shows beneath it but the flat panel of the face frame — the front of a head, and from there the surface of anything you turn outward.

音.story: Stand up and open your mouth wide enough that a whole sun rolls out of it — sound.
音.note: The lower box is a mouth with a stroke marking the noise inside, not 日 (sun); the sun is a hook.

風.story: A worm curls tight under the table while the gust tears past overhead — the old belief that the wind itself hatched the crawling things.
風.note: 几 is the remains of the phonetic 凡 and means nothing here.

飛.story: Two wings beating on either side of a body already climbing, feathers streaming back — flight caught mid-stroke.

食.story: A pedestrian bent low over a bowl of choice grain and not looking up until it is gone — eating.

首.story: Whiskers bristling above a nose, and under them the stalk holding the whole face up — the neck.

修.story: A standing person held straight as a pole, taking the whip until every hair lies in one even stroke — mending yourself into shape.
修.note: These four are shape-parts (攸 is the real phonetic), so take the scene as a hook rather than etymology.

個.story: One standing person shut up inside his own stronghold, separate and countable — an individual.
個.note: 固 was chosen for its コ sound; the stronghold is a hook.

倍.story: A standing person watches a split seed come apart and two stand where one did — doubled.
倍.note: 咅 is phonetic (バイ); the split seed is a hook.

借.story: The standing person is still using the thing he was lent back in olden days — borrowed, technically.
借.note: 昔 is here for its シャク sound only and has nothing to do with the past.

値.story: Ask the standing person what it costs and he hands you the straight number, no haggling — the price, the actual worth.
値.note: 直 supplies the sound (チ); the straightness is a hook.

倫.story: File each standing person like a bamboo slip, every strip in its proper order — that ordering of people is ethics.

勉.story: Throw every muscle into it just to escape the thing — the grinding effort we politely call diligence.

原.story: At the foot of the cliff a small white spring wells up — the source, and the wide plain it runs out across.

員.story: One mouth to feed for every cowrie shell on the payroll — each a counted member of the staff.

夏.story: A masked skull swaying above a trailing foot, stamping out the slow dance in the heat — summer.

娘.story: The young woman of the house, the choice grain of the whole family — the daughter.

宴.story: Under the roof a sunny woman keeps the cups going long past dark — the banquet.

家.story: The pig sleeps under the same roof as everybody else — that is exactly what makes it a house.

容.story: Put a whole valley under one roof and you have something that will hold anything you pour into it — containing.

将.story: Pinch the map flat on the camp bed and decide what happens at dawn — the general.
将.note: 丬 is the phonetic (ショウ); the bed is a memory hook only.

展.story: A corpse laid across a hurdle, a bent nail pinning one corner, a slash and a right sweep tugging the cloth open — the whole length unfolded for viewing.
展.note: The strokes below 尸 are shape-parts of a worn-down older form, not meaningful components.

島.story: One mountain coming straight up out of open water with nothing else attached to it — an island.
島.note: Only 山 is given here; the rest of the shape is a reduced 鳥 (bird), so lean on the lone peak.

差.story: No two sheep horns ever match: lay a carpenter's square across them and the slash of daylight underneath is the difference.

師.story: Rows of students drawn up in a girdle right around the earth mound, every face turned inward to the one figure at the centre — the teacher.

席.story: Under the lean-to, twenty towels laid out in a row — one seat for each guest.

帯.story: A picket fence of tassels, a crown of cloth, and the towel hanging down the front — the sash cinched round your middle.

帰.story: Prop the pole in the corner, drag the broom across the floor in one last slash, and go home.

座.story: Squat down on the packed earth under the lean-to — that spot is where you sit.

算.story: An eye runs down the rows of bamboo rods propped up on their stilts, tallying as it goes.
算.note: The 目+廾 is a flattened 具 (tool); read eye and stilts as shape-hooks.

管.story: Hollow out a length of bamboo, hand it to the bureaucrat, and now water, air and orders all flow through his pipe.
管.note: 官 (bureaucrat) is here for its カン sound; only the bamboo actually says pipe.

精.story: Rice polished past the husk down to the pale blue heart of the grain, and what is left is pure spirit.
精.note: 青 (blue) supplies the セイ sound; the rice carries the refining.

緒.story: Someone worries at a tangled skein until one loose thread comes free, and that tip is where the cord — and the work — begins.
緒.note: 者 (someone) is pure ショ sound; the thread does the meaning.

練.story: Raw thread boiled, beaten and hung out east-facing morning after morning until it is soft, strong and finally usable — repetition is what practice means.
練.note: The right side is a flattened 柬, not 東; treat east as a shape-hook only.

罰.story: Caught in the net, sentenced by words, marked with the blade: three stages of one penalty.

聞.story: An ear pressed to the crack in the gate, drinking in every word from the far side.

製.story: Cloth cut under strict control and stitched into a garment — nothing homemade about it, this is manufacture.

複.story: Inside the cloak a second cloak is sewn, the two layers puffing like a bellows as you walk: one garment, duplicated.
複.note: 复 rides along for its フク sound; 'bellows' is the shape you see, not a claim about meaning.

認.story: Jaw clenched, you endure every word across the table until your own head starts nodding — and that nod is you acknowledging it.

誘.story: Words that bloom so sweetly you find yourself following them straight out the door.
誘.note: 秀 (bloom) lends the ユウ sound and strictly says nothing about temptation.

語.story: Words coming out of five mouths at once, every one of them agreeing on the same sounds: a language.

誤.story: Confident words about the Wu kingdom from a man who has never once set foot there — wrong on every point.
誤.note: 呉 (wu kingdom) is pure ゴ sound, a memory-hook and nothing else.

説.story: Words handed over one at a time with a grin, until the listener's frown unknots and he finally sees what you meant.

読.story: Words hawked off a broadsheet the way a vendor sells fish, read aloud to everyone passing.
読.note: 売 (sell) is a simplified stand-in carrying the ドク/トク sound, not the meaning.

適.story: Take the road out to where the root stalk was planted and you find you have arrived at exactly the right spot.
適.note: 啇 (root stalk) supplies テキ only; the road carries the going-to sense.

銀.story: Cousin to gold but never gold, the paler metal that the stubborn eye keeps coming back to.
銀.note: 艮 (stubborn eye) is the sound; 金 does all the meaning work.

関.story: A gate barred for the night with a lit torch beside it, and nobody passes without stating their business.

際.story: The festival is pitched exactly where the hill runs out and the next land begins — the edge, and the one occasion the two sides meet on it.

隠.story: Behind the hill a claw closes over one small heart and tucks it out of sight.

雑.story: Nine small birds squabbling in a single sapling, a mixed and noisy assortment of whatever turned up.
雑.note: The modern shape is a squashed 雜 (衣 + 集); nine and sapling are shape-hooks, not meaning.

需.story: Rain running off an old man's beard as he stands in the field waiting for it, because the crop demands it now.
需.note: 而 (beard) is a corrupted remnant; the rain is the honest half of this character.

領.story: The head that issues the orders leans over the map and draws a line, and everything inside that line is his territory.

駅.story: Fresh horses waiting every so many yardsticks down the highway — the relay post, and now the train station.
駅.note: 尺 (yardstick) is a simplified stand-in for 睪 and carries only the エキ sound.

鳴.story: Open the bird's mouth and the whole valley fills with the sound.

鼻.story: The ancient nose sign hoisted up on an offering stand, planted dead center of the face where nobody can miss it.
鼻.note: 自 was itself the original nose pictograph; the stand below only supplies the ビ sound.

審.story: Under the roof, each case is taken in turn and picked apart until every last detail is plain.

寮.story: One roof, one bonfire, and everybody who sleeps there gathered around it.
寮.note: 尞 (bonfire) supplies the リョウ sound; the roof holds the meaning.

導.story: A thumb jabbed at the milestone: this way, keep up.

幣.story: Strips of tattered cloth and a folded towel handed over at the shrine, back when cloth served as both offering and currency.

徹.story: The whip cracks to raise the boy and drive him down the sidewalk with no stopping until he comes out the far end.
徹.note: 育 here is a worn-down 鬲 (cauldron); take 'raise' as a shape-hook.

慰.story: Run the flat iron over a creased heart and watch the wrinkles go out of it.

摩.story: A gloved hand works a bundle of hemp back and forth until the fibers lie smooth.
摩.note: 麻 (hemp) is chiefly there for the マ sound; the glove is what means rub.

撲.story: Fingers close around a fistful of brushwood and bring it down flat and hard.
撲.note: 菐 (brushwood) is pure ボク sound.

暫.story: The guillotine comes down through the daylight and lops off one short slice of sun.
暫.note: 斬 (guillotine) carries the ザン sound; the sun is what makes this about time.

横.story: A yellow-barked tree laid flat across the gateposts, and now everything about it reads sideways.
横.note: 黄 (yellow) is the オウ sound and nothing more.

潔.story: Water droplets run the whole length of the measuring cord until not one fiber of it is dirty.

熱.story: A fresh planting set straight over the cooking fire, its leaves already curling in the heat.

監.story: The minister, hairpin still in place, leans over one dish of still water and studies what looks back — nothing gets past him.

確.story: A hooded hawk perched on solid stone, neither of them moving: about as sure a thing as you will get.
確.note: 隺 (hooded hawk) supplies the カク sound; the stone is where the certainty lives.

線.story: One thread of water leaves the fountain and runs downhill in a single unbroken line.

締.story: Thread drawn tight around the parcel and knotted under the emperor's seal, and now it stays shut.
締.note: 帝 (emperor) is the テイ sound; the thread does the tightening.

舞.story: Hairpin fixed, dance plumes fanned in both hands, feet crossing like a turnstile, the whole figure balanced on one spot and spinning.
舞.note: 舞 is really one pictograph of a dancer holding plumes; the listed parts are fragments of that single shape.

衝.story: Something heavy comes off the sidewalk into the right lane at full speed, and the two meet.
衝.note: 重 (heavy) is mainly the ショウ sound; the street radical carries the meaning.

課.story: The office where words go out in the morning and fruit is expected back by evening: your section, your lesson, your quota.
課.note: 果 (fruit) mostly supplies the カ sound.

調.story: Words carried the full circumference of a thing, checking every side, then nudging it until it rings true.

談.story: Words traded back and forth across twin flames long after the meal has been cleared.
談.note: 炎 (twin flames) rides in for the ダン sound; the warmth is a bonus, not etymology.

論.story: Words filed in strict order like bamboo slips bound edge to edge — the ordering is what turns a rant into an argument.

賛.story: Twin husbands step up together and push a single cowrie shell across the table between them — the loudest way there is to say you approve.

質.story: Axe weighed against axe, and both against a cowrie shell, to settle what the metal is really worth.
質.note: The paired axes chiefly supply the sound; the cowrie shell is what speaks to worth.

趣.story: What you run toward when nobody is making you, and take for your own — that is a person's taste.
趣.note: 取 (take) is largely the シュ sound here.

選.story: A kneeling pair waits by the road while you walk the line and take exactly one of them.
選.note: 巽 (kneeling pair) supplies the セン sound rather than a meaning.

遺.story: Treasure set down on the road behind you as you walk on, left there for whoever comes after.

凝.story: A question mark hangs over the puddle while the ice creeps in from the edges and the whole thing sets hard before you get your answer.
凝.note: 疑 (question mark) is pure sound here; the ice does the congealing.

整.story: An edict comes down and every last thing is dressed straight against the tally mark.

扶.story: The husband is buckling under the beam, so your fingers close on the far end and take half its weight — that is aid.

技.story: What separates the trained hand from the untrained one: fingers that can walk a branch across the knuckles without dropping it — skill.

把.story: The fingers close the way a python closes, coil after coil, until nothing can slip out — a grasp.

投.story: Wind the war club back past your ear, then open the fingers at the top of the arc and let it go — throw.

択.story: Every candidate gets held up against the yardstick, and only then do the fingers close on one — choose.
択.note: 尺 is a postwar stand-in for the original 睪; treat it as the sound cue タク, not a real part of the meaning.

改.story: The whip lands on nobody but your own self, and by morning yesterday's habit has been beaten into a better shape.

攻.story: Run a carpenter's square along the wall to find the weak seam, then bring the whip down exactly there — a measured attack.

更.story: One more pass of the scythe after the sun is down, the same field started over again — the work renews itself and the night wears late.

材.story: A crowbar levers the felled tree up onto the cart, because timber only becomes material once someone hauls it out.
材.note: 才 is here purely for the sound ザイ; the crowbar image is a hook, not etymology.

村.story: Count the houses off on your thumb, one per tree along the single lane, and you have counted the whole village.

束.story: The character draws exactly what it means: sticks gathered upright with a band cinched round the middle, a bundle you could carry under one arm.

条.story: A trailing foot drags one stripped branch away from the tree — a single clean stripe of wood, and by the same logic a single numbered article of the law.

来.story: Picture the wheat plant this shape once drew, ears hanging left and right, and remember that the grain is what came to you.
来.note: 来 is a pictograph of a wheat plant borrowed purely for its sound; the meaning 'come' has no connection to grain.

求.story: One bowl held out under the splash, not surrendering a single crumb of what falls — the posture of a man asking.

決.story: The archer's ring slips, the dyke gives, and the water droplets are through the gap before anyone can argue it back — that irreversible instant is deciding.

没.story: A war club goes over the side of the boat: a scatter of water droplets, then nothing at all — it has sunk.

沢.story: Push a yardstick down through the reeds and it keeps going, water droplets and black mud all the way — a swamp.
沢.note: 尺 replaced the original 睪 in the postwar shape and only carries the sound タク.

況.story: Your older brother squats at the bank reading the water droplets — colour, speed, depth — and then tells you how things actually stand.
況.note: 兄 contributes only the sound キョウ; the brother is a memory image.

状.story: A dog sprawled on its bed, and the shape it has folded itself into tells you its whole condition at a glance.
状.note: 丬 is a phonetic element (ジョウ) here, not a meaning; the bed is a hook.

男.story: Muscle spent on the rice paddy from first light to last — in the old writing, that was the entire definition of a man.

町.story: Nails driven at the corners of the rice paddy to fix the boundaries, and the grid of parcels between them grows into a town.

社.story: A shrine raised over the mound of soil where the local god lives, because the village gathers there — and the gathering is now what you call your company.

私.story: A grain stalk hooked in tight against your own elbow: this sheaf is mine, nobody else's — and from that hoarding comes the word for I.

究.story: Nine turns deeper into the cave and your hand finally hits the back wall — that stubborn crawl to the end is research.
究.note: 九 supplies the sound キュウ only; the nine turns are a memory device.

系.story: A slash of the hand lifts a single thread and the whole hank comes up with it, knot following knot — a lineage.

良.story: A stubborn eye sights down the pole the whole length of it, and passes it only when the thing is dead straight and good.
良.note: 艮 + 丨 is a shape-level breakdown of the modern form, not real etymology — 良 originally depicted a device for rinsing grain clean.

花.story: Somewhere up in the flowers a shapeshifter is at work, turning a tight green knot into an open bloom overnight.
花.note: 化 mainly carries the sound カ; the transformation reading is a convenient hook rather than the historical logic.

見.story: An eye mounted on a pair of legs, so it can walk itself over and get a proper look.

言.story: Lines stacking up out of the opening at the base, breath drawn as though you could see it leaving — words, said aloud.

谷.story: Two slopes fall away left and right to a narrow gap at the bottom, and that pinch is where the stream runs — a valley.

赤.story: Iron-heavy soil baked all summer until the whole hillside glows red.
赤.note: 赤 doesn't genuinely decompose this way — 土 is just the piece of the modern shape you can hold onto; the original drew a person over a fire.

走.story: Soil kicked up in a rooster-tail behind a striding foot — you can tell someone is running from the dust alone.

足.story: The striding foot below and the round mouth of the kneecap above make one whole leg — and a leg that gets you there is enough.

身.story: A silhouette in profile with the belly swelled out — a body carrying something, which is why it also means oneself and one's station.

車.story: Look straight down on an ox-cart: one axle running through, the box in the middle, a wheel at either end.

迎.story: Instead of waiting indoors you go out along the road to where the supplicant is standing and bring him in yourself — that walk is what welcome means.

近.story: A stretch of road short enough to carry an axe the whole way without once setting it down — near.

返.story: Halfway down the road you flip on your heel and carry the borrowed thing back where it came from.

並.story: Whiskers combed flat across a bell rack, every prong at the same height, nothing sticking out — things lined up in a row and therefore all thoroughly ordinary.
並.note: 䒑 and 业 are shape-level pieces of the modern form; 並 was originally two people standing side by side.

事.story: One long flagpole held upright through the middle of everything, all day, because somebody has to — whatever you are stuck holding up is the matter at hand.

京.story: A lid of a roof, a mouth of a gate below it, and small pillars holding the whole thing clear of the ground — the great hall you can see from any street in the capital.

使.story: The standing person spends the entire day running the clerk's errands, which is to say he is being used.

例.story: One standing person steps forward out of the row so everybody can see exactly what is meant — an example.

供.story: Both hands together, the standing person lifts it to eye level and holds it out without flinching — an offering.

依.story: Swallowed by a garment two sizes too big, the standing person leans his whole weight into it to stay upright — relying on it.

価.story: Every crate hauled in under the west cap goes to the standing person at the desk, and the number he chalks on the side is its value.
価.note: 覀 is a postwar squashing of 賈 (merchant); read it as a shape hook, not as 'west'.

具.story: One eye runs across the rack — eight pegs, every tool hanging where it belongs, nothing missing and everything equipped.
具.note: The 目 on top is a flattened bronze vessel in the original, and 八 the two hands holding it; the eye-and-rack scene is a memory image.

制.story: Under the awning the cow is broken down to a fixed pattern, the blade taking the same cuts in the same order every single time — that ruled procedure is a system.

券.story: Kneading hands press the agreement flat and a cleaver splits it straight down the middle — the half you walk away with is your ticket.

効.story: Muscle applied with the crossed legs braced hard against the floor, because force only counts once it lands — and 交 hands over its コウ on the way.
効.note: 交 is purely phonetic (コウ); the braced stance is a hook, not the character's real logic.

卒.story: Lapels stitched with a ten to show the full term has been served — the soldier is finished and walks out a graduate.

協.story: Three muscles hauling on one rope with ten more pairs of hands behind them, everyone pulling on the same count — cooperation.

参.story: A big man, elbow crooked in salute and hair oiled into three glossy stripes for the occasion, presents himself at the shrine gate.
参.note: 参 originally drew three stars over a kneeling figure; 厶, 大 and 彡 are handles on the modern shape rather than the true parts.

取.story: The right hand closes on an ear and pulls — ancient soldiers were paid by the ears they took.

受.story: A claw lowers the thing over a crown-shaped lid into the right hand waiting underneath — the exact instant of receiving.

習.story: Feathers beating the same stroke a thousand times against a white sky — nobody is born flying, you drill it.
習.note: 白 contributes only shape and sound here; the repetition sense is all in 羽.

船.story: A boat that has outgrown the marsh it was built in — ribbed, decked, and ready for open water.
船.note: 㕣 is the phonetic element; the marsh is a memory image, not part of the meaning.

著.story: Someone standing shoulder-deep in flowers whose head still shows above every bloom — remarkable enough that people write the name down.
著.note: 者 supplies the sound チョ only; the meaning rides on 艹.

術.story: Millet threshed the same exact way on the sidewalk and again in the right lane — a method so repeatable it becomes an art.
術.note: 朮 is purely phonetic; the millet is a hook, and 彳+亍 are the two halves of the 行 road.

規.story: The husband squints down the length of the board and sees at a glance that it is out of true — his eye is the standard the work is held to.
規.note: Whether 夫 here means a grown man or is a worn-down phonetic is genuinely disputed.

訪.story: Words called up under the household's banner before you cross the threshold — the polite noise a visit makes, riding 方's ホウ.
訪.note: 方 is the phonetic only; a banner has nothing to do with visiting.

設.story: Words give the order and the war club drives the first post into the ground — that is how a thing gets set up.

許.story: The petitioner kneels there all morning, and at noon the words finally come down from the bench: permitted.
許.note: 午 carries sound, not sense; noon is a peg to hang the shape on.

訳.story: Words laid flat against a yardstick and measured across into another language — along with the reason behind every choice you made.
訳.note: 尺 here is a worn-down phonetic standing in for 睪; it is not really a ruler.

転.story: The car's wheels spin so hard a vapor curl lifts off the tarmac — rolling, turning, and one bad camber from tipping over.
転.note: 云 is a simplification of the old phonetic 專 and means nothing here.

週.story: Take the road the whole way around the circumference and you come back out at Monday — one week.

部.story: Crack the hill open and you find it packed like a split seed — every section already parcelled off into its own wedge.
部.note: 咅 is the phonetic; the split seed is an image, not a meaning.

郵.story: At the last hill town on the frontier road the courier's bag droops off his shoulder and a fresh rider swings it onto his own — the postal relay.

都.story: Someone, and someone, and someone again, all crowding onto the same hill until that town outgrows every other in the country — the capital.
都.note: 者 gives the sound ト; the crowd reading is a hook.

釈.story: Set a yardstick beside the paw print and you can explain exactly what came through here — then let the animal go.
釈.note: 尺 replaces the old phonetic 睪 and carries no measuring sense.

野.story: Past the last village the ground unrolls like a yo-yo dropped and never wound back — open field all the way to the horizon.
野.note: 予 is strictly the phonetic ヤ; the yo-yo is a shape mnemonic.

閉.story: A crowbar shoved crosswise through the gate's handles — nothing is opening tonight.
閉.note: The inner stroke is a drawn bolt that happens to look like 才.

魚.story: Beak-shaped head on top, a rice paddy of scales for the flank, and the cooking fire's four dots fanned out as the tail — a fish, nose to fin.
魚.note: 魚 is a pictograph; 田 and 灬 are only the shapes the body and tail settled into.

鳥.story: Crest, eye, and folded wing seen from the side, with the cooking fire's four dots hanging beneath as tail feathers.
鳥.note: A pictograph — 灬 is the only nameable piece, and here it draws tail feathers, not fire.

黒.story: Cooking fire smoking under the village night after night until every beam is soot-cured through — black.
黒.note: The upper part is historically a soot-caked chimney; 里 is the modern shape only.

偉.story: A standing person in tanned leather that cost a whole herd and a year of work to earn — the sort of figure a room gets up for.
偉.note: 韋 is the phonetic イ; leather says nothing about greatness.

備.story: Ahead of the storm the standing person has driven twin stakes into the cliff face and hung the bucket ready on them.
備.note: The right half is a worn-down quiver of arrows; 卄, 厂 and 用 are the pieces it broke into.

割.story: Harm done on purpose, with a blade, along a line agreed beforehand — the whole thing comes apart into shares.
割.note: 害 is the phonetic カツ, though the violence of it reads conveniently well.

勝.story: Toil going on under the moon long after the other side has gone to bed — that is what a win is actually made of.
勝.note: 月 here is the flesh radical and 劵 is a sound element; the moonlit-toil scene is a hook, not etymology.

勤.story: Flowers tied up the trellis, a mouth at home waiting to be fed, and the muscle to be back out here again tomorrow.
勤.note: The left side is the phonetic 堇; 艹, 口 and 龶 are its broken-up parts, not meanings.

喜.story: A drum pounded hard with a mouth wide open beneath it, hollering along with every beat — rejoicing.

報.story: Handcuffs snapped shut on the captive, and the runner sprints back to the fort with the report — and collects the reward.

場.story: Bare soil with sunbeams lying flat across it and nothing blocking any side — the open ground where things happen.

奥.story: Past a slash of curtain and under the awning, big sacks of rice sit stacked in the one room guests never see.
奥.note: The modern shape is opaque; 丿, 冂, 米 and 大 are strokes it fell into, not an original composition.

富.story: A granary that fits under your own roof, full to the rafters — that is what wealth actually looks like.

寒.story: Packed straw jammed into every crack in the wall, and icicles forming on the inside anyway.

就.story: You turn up in the capital with a blemish on your record and they hand you the office regardless — the post is yours.
就.note: The composition is opaque; 尤 functions as a sound element rather than a flaw.

幅.story: A towel unrolled flat along the granary wall and read off end to end — that span is its width.
幅.note: 畐 is the phonetic フク; the granary contributes nothing to the meaning.

廃.story: The lean-to after everyone's departure — poles leaning, roof gone through, left to fall in on itself.
廃.note: 発 is the phonetic here; the departure reading is a convenient hook.

悲.story: A heart grown split wings, each half beating away from the other, and that tearing is sadness.
悲.note: 非 is strictly the phonetic ヒ; the wings pulling apart are a memory image.

惑.story: The border guard's heart when the papers look right and the face looks wrong — perplexed, and one step from being taken in.
惑.note: 或 supplies the sound ワク only.

握.story: Fingers clamped on the shop's door pull, knuckles gone white, refusing to let it swing.
握.note: 屋 is the phonetic; a shop has nothing to do with gripping.

援.story: Fingers locked on the rope in a tug-of-war, hauling the man at the far end back up onto solid ground.

揺.story: Fingers on one side, a claw on the other, and the clay jar rocking back and forth between them.
揺.note: The right side is a phonetic; 爫 and 𠙻 are the shapes it decomposes into.

敬.story: The whip comes down every time the grass phrase is fumbled, until the boy recites it with something like respect.
敬.note: 苟 is the phonetic ケイ; the phrase-being-drilled image is a hook.

晩.story: The sun makes its escape behind the ridge and takes the whole day with it.
晩.note: 免 gives only the sound バン.

普.story: Sun striking both of the twin pillars at exactly the same angle, and everything behind them too — light that plays no favorites.
普.note: 並 functions as the phonetic; the even-handedness of two matched pillars is a mnemonic bonus.

暑.story: Sun straight overhead and someone underneath it with no shade for a mile in any direction.
暑.note: 者 is purely the phonetic ショ.

替.story: Twin husbands hand the shift over under the same sun — one walks off, the other walks straight on.
替.note: The bottom was originally 曰 (speak), not 日; the sun is the modern shape only.

最.story: Reach up and take the sun itself — there is nothing left that you could possibly take more of.
最.note: The top element was originally a helmet (冒), not the sun.

朝.story: The dawn thicket is already lit up while the moon still hangs over it, too slow to leave — morning.

期.story: Drop the moons into the winnowing basket one by one and count them out — what you have measured is a fixed period.
期.note: 其 is the phonetic キ; the basket is a counting image only.

森.story: Set one more tree on top of an entire grove and you have stopped counting trunks — forest.

極.story: The ridgepole tree with a pressed man wedged between beam and floor, straining at the very last inch there is.
極.note: 亟 is the phonetic キョク; the man under pressure is a hook that happens to fit.

歯.story: A pit of an open mouth with rice-grain rows set into it, and a footprint stamped above marking where the food stops.
歯.note: 止 sits on top for sound (シ); the pit and grains are the original picture of a mouthful of teeth.

減.story: Every war cry from the parched line costs another mouthful, and the water droplets left in the canteen only ever go down.
減.note: 咸 is the phonetic; the shouting is a memory image.

渡.story: The measuring hand checks how deep the water droplets run at the ford, then you cross and hand the pole to whoever is next.

温.story: Water droplets left standing all afternoon in a sunlit dish — warm to the finger, never hot.

港.story: Water droplets filling the alleys between the piers with a boat nosed into each one — a town whose streets are made of water.
港.note: 巷 carries the sound コウ; the alley image happens to suit the berths.

湖.story: Water droplets pooled so wide that the barbarian waving from the far shore is only a smudge.
湖.note: 胡 is the phonetic コ and says nothing about water.

心.story: Three drops flick off a slack pouch of muscle: the heart, with every mood the mind hangs on it.

戸.story: Lay a corpse flat, stand it up, cap it with one plank, and you have the single-leaf door a household swings shut at night.

手.story: Peel the glove off and the shape stays behind: four fingers splayed above a wrist, a hand.

支.story: A right hand clamps around a ten and holds it upright, propping up everything that would otherwise sag.

文.story: Under the lid, a scythe scores its crossed mark into wet clay, and a row of those marks read straight through is a sentence.

方.story: Lid on top, a slash to one side, and a crane arm swinging out over the yard: whichever way that arm points is the direction you go.

日.story: A disc with a mark burnt through the middle is the sun, and one whole turn of it is a day.

月.story: Two clouds cross a thin crescent; the moon takes one full filling and emptying to make a month.

木.story: One upright stroke with limbs flung up and roots braced out into the dirt: a tree holding its ground.

比.story: Two crouching figures tucked one behind the other, identical down to the elbow, daring you not to compare them.

水.story: A barb of current down the middle, an eyebrow of foam hooked off it, a slash flying left and a right sweep flying right: water breaking around a rock.

火.story: Eight sparks jump off the log and the pedestrian leaps back from the fire.

父.story: Eight children scatter the moment father swings the scythe up onto his shoulder.

片.story: A plank sawn straight down the grain with only the split half on the right still standing: one side of the board and nothing else.

牛.story: Two horns, the left hitched higher than the right, sit over a long bony face that never quite squares up to you: a cow.

世.story: Three uprights lashed to a single crossbar count out three decades, one generation, and the whole world it hands on.

主.story: The lid burns like a flame above a column of packed soil, the one lamp in the hall, and whoever owns that hall is the master.

仕.story: A standing person spends the whole day at the samurai's elbow, fetching tea and bowing, which is what it is to serve.

他.story: A standing person keeps a scorpion between himself and you: everything on that side of it belongs to the other.
他.note: 也 (scorpion) is here purely for its sound (タ) and contributes nothing to the meaning; the standing person carries 'other person'.

付.story: A thumb presses the label flat against a standing person's back, and now it is attached to him.

代.story: The standing person walks off his post, leaving a stake driven into the ground to hold it as his substitute.

以.story: Nobody turns a field with bare hands; you turn it by means of the plow.
以.note: 以 does not decompose in this system and its origin is disputed; 'plow' is a shape hook, not an etymology.

兄.story: The mouth mounted on a pair of legs belongs to the older brother, who has been telling everyone shorter than him what to do since birth.

写.story: Slip a clean sheet under the crown and let the page above give its ink down to it, making a copy.

冬.story: A trailing foot drags home over two icicles at the frozen tail of the year: winter.

出.story: A sprout shoves up out of the pit and clears the rim, out at last.

功.story: Pour muscle into work laid out by the carpenter's square until the thing actually stands, and that standing thing is your merit.

加.story: Add a mouth to the muscle already hauling and the crew has grown by one.

北.story: Two spoons sit back to back, each refusing to face the other, and the direction you keep your back turned to is north.

半.story: Horns above, two lines below, and a pole rammed straight down between them splits the carcass in half.

去.story: One elbow shoves off the soil and the man is up and gone, already in the past.

古.story: This story passed through ten mouths before it reached yours, and it was old when it started.

句.story: Wrap one mouthful of speech inside a bracket and stop there: a single phrase.

可.story: The mouth says yes and a nail pins that yes down so it cannot wriggle: permitted, possible, go ahead.

台.story: Stack an elbow squarely on top of a mouth, two blocks one above the other, and you have the low stand a speaker climbs onto to be seen.

史.story: The scribe's brush, held dead centre and driven straight down the page, pins each reign and famine into history.

右.story: A left hand curves over a mouth to feed it, except the hand that actually holds the chopsticks is the right one.
右.note: 𠂇 is the generic hand-shape primitive that this system names 'left hand'; it makes no claim about direction here, so 右 and 左 have to be learned as a contrasting pair.

号.story: A mouth bellows over a bent cane, calling out the next number in the queue.

司.story: A crane arm swings out over a capped mouth: orders issued from behind a screen, which is an officer's entire job.

四.story: Legs penned inside a city wall that has, count them, four sides.
四.note: 四 was borrowed for its sound; the original 'four' was simply four stacked strokes, so the city wall and legs are a memory hook only.

外.story: The divining rod belongs to the morning; cast it in the evening and you are out in the dark yard, outside.

央.story: A figure with a bar across the shoulders and arms flung wide stands exactly where that bar balances: dead center.

失.story: A slash cuts across the husband's arm and whatever he was holding is already on the floor, lost.

左.story: The left hand pins the carpenter's square while the other hand does the sawing.

市.story: A towel hung from a crossbar-shaped lid makes one shop banner, and a hundred more down the street make the market that grew into a city.

布.story: The left hand snaps a towel open and lets it settle flat across the counter: a bolt of cloth.

平.story: A shield laid face up with its horns trimmed level on both sides, flat enough to stand a cup on.

広.story: Under the lean-to sits one elbow's worth of furniture and nothing else, so the floor just runs away, wide and empty.

弁.story: An elbow cranks a lever mounted on stilts, opening the valve and shutting it again.
弁.note: Modern 弁 merges four unrelated older characters (valve, speech/argue, petal, manage), so the elbow-on-stilts image is a hook for the shape, not the etymology of any one sense.

必.story: A slash driven clean through the heart: some things are certain, and your feelings get no vote.

打.story: Fingers snap down flat on the nail head hard enough to sting, one clean hit.
打.note: 丁 supplies only the sound here (ダ); the fingers are what make this 'hit'.

未.story: The zodiac sheep's sign is a sapling whose topmost branch is still shorter than the one below it: growth that has not yet arrived.
未.note: The 'zodiac sheep' label comes from a sound borrowing — the sheep has nothing to do with 'not yet'.

末.story: A bar laid flat across the treetop, wider than any branch beneath it, marks how far the tree goes: the end.

本.story: A stroke cut low across the trunk points at the root of the matter, the origin you trace everything back to, and so the book you open to find it.

札.story: A slip of tree wood hangs on a fishhook by the gate with a name inked on it: a tag, and in your wallet, a bill.
札.note: 乚 is a sound element only (サツ); the wood is what makes this a tag.

庭.story: A lean-to propped along one wall, the court opening out in front of it — that enclosed strip of ground is the garden.

弱.story: Leave two bows out overnight and the ice glazing each one turns good strong wood weak.

恋.story: Heart hammering, armpits soaked through, the body confesses love a good minute before the mouth does.

恥.story: The heart knows first, but it is the ear that goes scarlet and publishes your shame to the room.

息.story: Nose above heart, and the breath running between the two is what keeps the whole arrangement going.

挙.story: Up goes the glove with the candelabra still in it, held over the crowd so nobody can miss it.

振.story: Fingers clamped on a dragon's tail get shaken hard for their trouble.
振.note: 辰 is here only for the sound シン; the dragon is a memory hook, not part of the meaning.

料.story: Rice struck level in the dipper: measure out the ingredients, then name the fee.

旅.story: Up goes the banner, and behind it a column of hairpin-topped heads sets off down the road.

既.story: A belch so final that nobody at the table needs telling the meal is already over.
既.note: Only the right-hand 旡 is broken out here — a diner turning from the table with a belch. Treat it as the whole picture.

時.story: The sun sliding across the temple roof is the only clock the village needs, and it carries 寺's ジ along with it.

書.story: The brush hand lays down one stroke above the sun, and there is your word, written in plain daylight.

校.story: Benches cut from one tree, a pair of crossed legs tucked under every single one: school, riding 交's コウ.

根.story: Down beneath the tree a stubborn eye stares into the dirt and refuses to be pulled up.

格.story: Behind the welcome mat stands a tree of pigeonholes, one slot per guest, assigned strictly by rank.

残.story: The twin halberds finished their work by noon; what remains on the field at dusk is bones.

流.story: An inverted child swept along headfirst by water droplets — everything traveling one direction only, which is flow.

浜.story: Soldiers form up in a line exactly where the water droplets stop, boots planted on the sand of the beach.
浜.note: 兵 is a postwar stand-in for 賓 and supplies only the sound; the soldier means nothing here.

浪.story: Choice grain heaped into long rolling ridges, and past the sand the water droplets are heaped the same way, wave after wave.
浪.note: 良 carries the ロウ sound and no meaning; the grain is a hook.

浴.story: Stand in the valley where the water droplets come down off the rock and take the whole cold column on your shoulders: a bath.

消.story: Water droplets whittle the flame down to one last sliver, then swallow even that, and the light is out.

特.story: One cow lives at the temple, never yoked, hand-fed for the festival, and that is what makes it special.

留.story: A cleaver driven into the post at the edge of the rice paddy: nobody leaves, everything stays put.

疲.story: Draped over the sickbed limp as a wet pelt hung on a rail, too tired to lift a hand.
疲.note: 皮 is there for the ヒ sound; the pelt is a memory image, not a meaning component.

病.story: The sickbed goes up on a sawhorse in the middle of the room, because this has stopped being a nap and become an illness.
病.note: 丙 is purely phonetic; the sawhorse carries no meaning of its own.

症.story: Beside the sickbed, one fresh tally mark chalked up for every new symptom.
症.note: 正 supplies the ショウ sound; the tally mark is a hook, not the character's logic.

真.story: Ten different tools measure the same board and all ten agree, which is what truth looks like.

眠.story: At the end of a long day the commoner's eye slides shut without asking anyone's permission.
眠.note: 民 gives only the ミン sound; the commoner adds nothing to the meaning.

破.story: Throw a stone hard enough and it goes clean through the stretched pelt, tearing the whole thing open.
破.note: 皮 is chiefly the ハ sound; the pelt is a serviceable image rather than the real semantics.

秘.story: There is one grain stalk you show nobody, its name pierced into your heart and kept there.
秘.note: An opaque one: 禾 stands in for an older 示 (altar), and 必 supplies the sound. The story is a hook, not etymology.

笑.story: A dancer doubled over and whipping back upright like a bamboo stalk in wind, helpless with laughter.

紋.story: Writing done in thread instead of ink, stitched at the shoulder of the coat, is the family crest.

紙.story: Thread is pulped, pressed flat, and stamped with the clan's mark to come out as a sheet of paper.
紙.note: 氏 is present for the シ sound only; the clan mark is a mnemonic addition.

能.story: Bear snout out front, two spoons behind it for paws: the beast that can do absolutely anything, hence ability.

脅.story: Three muscles flexed an inch from your face under a bare moon say everything a threat needs to say.
脅.note: 月 here is the flesh radical (ribs, the side of the body), not the moon, and 劦 mainly carries キョウ.

般.story: Poled along by the war club, the boat calls at every landing on the river and takes on all sorts.

荷.story: You cannot see the porter at all under the flowers strapped to his back, only the load.

記.story: The self who was in the room writes the words down while they are still warm, and that page is the record.

財.story: A crowbar cracks the chest open and cowrie shells spill across the floor: wealth.

起.story: The serpent uncoils and you are off the floor and into a run before you have thought about it.

逐.story: A pig gets loose on the road and the whole village strings out behind it, one after another.

通.story: A pipe runs straight under the road with daylight showing at both ends, nothing in the way.

速.story: Strap the load into one tight bundle and you cover the road twice as fast.

連.story: Car behind car behind car on the same road, coupled bumper to bumper in one unbroken line.

配.story: Kneel by the sake jar yourself and work round the circle, filling every cup in turn.

酒.story: Water droplets beading on the cold flank of the sake jar in the cellar mean the liquor is ready.

降.story: Downhill feet come off the hill one careful step at a time.

院.story: Inside the hill of its boundary wall sits a finished house with gate and courtyard, an institution rather than a home.

馬.story: Mane flying above, and the four dots of cooking fire below are really four hooves at full gallop: a horse in profile.
馬.note: A pictograph. The 灬 is not fire at all here — it is the legs and tail — so treat the cooking fire purely as a shape hook.

高.story: A lid on top, a mouth for a window beneath it, all of it standing on a tower base far above the street.

側.story: A standing person at your elbow with the rulebook open, never once leaving your side.

偶.story: A standing person rounds the corner and walks straight into an ape, which absolutely nobody planned.
偶.note: 禺 supplies the グウ sound; the ape has no share in the meaning.

動.story: Something heavy, one muscle set against it, and at last the thing moves.

務.story: Halberd in your hands, whip at your back, muscle in your arms: the work you are obliged to do.

商.story: A lid over the stall, horns painted on the signboard, and a lattice window to haggle through, which is where the day's trade gets done.

正.story: Draw one line on the ground, then plant a footprint square on it: dead on the mark, exactly correct.

母.story: The graph refuses to come apart — read the two dots at its center as the nursing breasts of the mother the whole shape draws.

民.story: One undivided shape: a face with the eye struck through, the old brand of a commoner, and from that, the common people of a nation.
民.note: The blinded-slave account is the standard reading but not certain; the app treats this as one unbroken shape, not a composition.

氷.story: A pond with a single crumb of frost stuck to its edge, and by morning the whole surface has gone hard: ice.

汁.story: Crush anything hard enough and ten water droplets run out of it — juice in the glass, broth in the bowl.
汁.note: 十 is present for its ジュウ sound; counting to ten is a memory hook, not part of the meaning.

玄.story: Clamp a lid down over a skein nobody can find the loose end of — dark, deep, and not meant to be read.

玉.story: Hand the king one more crumb and it turns out to be the polished jewel he rolls between his fingers.

甘.story: One closed shape with a bar held across its middle: something is being kept on the tongue as long as possible because it is sweet.

生.story: The whole graph is a shoot breaking the surface and still climbing — birth, raw greenness, life before anything has been done to it.

用.story: An awning stiffened by two crossbars and one pole down the center: a frame built for nothing but use.

由.story: The whole shape is an oil jar with its spout pushing out the top; trace the flow back down into the vessel and you have found the reason.

申.story: Lightning cracks out of a clear sky and the entire village hears it at once — that is the register you use reporting upward to someone above you.

白.story: Read the whole graph as a lamp with the glare flaring off its top; everything that light touches is bleached white.

目.story: Stand the graph on end and it is the eye itself: a lid above, a lid below, the pupil ruled straight across the middle.

矛.story: A shark fin for the blade, a dangling hook for the tassel, one slash for the shaft — the halberd.

石.story: Under the hat brim of the ledge sits a mouth-sized lump you would stub a toe on: a stone.

礼.story: At the shrine you fold yourself into a fishhook, and holding that bow a second longer than strictly needed is courtesy.
礼.note: 乚 is postwar shorthand for the old right half (豊); it is a shape to hang the bow on, not a meaning.

立.story: Lid for a head, horns for shoulders, one flat line for the floor: a body holding itself upright.

込.story: The whole road trying to enter through one doorway at the same moment — packed in, crowded, nobody moving.

両.story: One bar laid over an awning, and beneath it a mountain sliced cleanly down the middle into matching halves: both sides, equal weight.

争.story: A beak bites down on one straight bar, a barb hooks the far end of the same bar, and neither will loosen its grip — the two of them compete over that single thing.

交.story: Father sits in his lid of a hat with his legs crossed at the ankle; where lines cross like that, people mix.

件.story: One standing person, one cow: livestock counted head by head is where the habit of counting matters and cases one at a time comes from.

任.story: The standing person shoulders the carrying pole, and everything swinging off both ends of it is now their responsibility.

企.story: Up on the toes of a footprint, the pedestrian cranes to see the far end of the road before taking a single step — that look ahead is the plan.

会.story: A pedestrian pitched like a tent over a vapor curl of warm breath: bodies packed close enough to fog the air, which is a meeting.

伝.story: The standing person hands off a vapor curl of rumor, it drifts to the next listener and the next, and somewhere along the line it becomes legend.

先.story: An ox head riding out in front of a pair of legs — the nose reaches the gate well ahead of the rest of the animal.

全.story: The pedestrian spreads over the king like a roof, leaving no corner of the realm uncovered: all of it, entire.

共.story: One hurdle, eight hands underneath it, nobody strong enough alone — so it goes up together.

印.story: Bear down on the kneeling man's back and the shape he leaves behind in the wax is the seal.
印.note: Only 卩 is in the given breakdown; the pressing hand on the left has no keyword here, so the kneeling man has to carry the whole image.

各.story: Every latecomer's trailing foot stops at the same mouth of the doorway and gets counted separately: each, one by one.

合.story: A tent dropped over a mouth, rim to rim, not a gap anywhere — things that fit are things that agree.

同.story: Every mouth under the one crossbeam saying the identical thing at the identical moment.

名.story: By evening nobody can make out who is at the door, so a mouth has to call out in the dark — that shout is your name.

向.story: A slash of light over the awning, a mouth of a window beneath it, and the whole house turned to face that way.

回.story: A single mouth boxed in by a city wall with no gate, so all you can do is walk the same loop again — and each lap counts as one time round.

因.story: A big man shut inside the city wall; what everyone wants to know is the reason he ended up in there — the cause.

在.story: Pull up the floorboards and there is soil underneath, sitting exactly where it has always sat, whether or not anyone went looking — it is there, it exists.
在.note: Only 土 is in the given breakdown; the upper-left element is phonetic (ザイ) and adds nothing to the meaning.

地.story: Soil with a scorpion running flat across it: the land underfoot, borrowing 也's チ as it goes.
地.note: 也 is purely phonetic here — the scorpion is a sound peg, not part of the meaning.

多.story: One evening stacked on another evening, and after that the nights pile up faster than anyone bothers to count.

字.story: A child kept under the roof, drilling strokes on paper until each written character finally comes out right.

宅.story: A roof propped up on one bent stalk of a post — small, standing, and yours: the residence you go home to.
宅.note: 乇 supplies the タク sound; the bent stalk is a picture to hang the roof on, not a meaning.

安.story: A woman settled under her own roof with nothing to fear and nothing to pay: at ease, and therefore cheap.

寺.story: A patch of soil measured off by the thumb and set aside for official use — which is exactly what the ground under a temple started out as.

州.story: Three humps of silt standing up out of the current: sandbars solid enough to build on, and eventually to call a province.

年.story: Take the shape whole: a body stooped under an armful of cut grain, hauling in one harvest, which is one year.
年.note: Given here as a single unbroken shape — the stooped-harvester image is a memory hook, not a breakdown you can reuse elsewhere.

式.story: A carpenter's square hanging on the ceremonial stake: everything done to the set measure, in the set order.
式.note: 弋 is there for its シキ sound; the stake contributes nothing to the meaning.

当.story: A tuft of hair standing straight up on the snout, right where the dart went in — a direct hit.
当.note: The modern shape is a postwar simplification of 當; tuft and snout are a memory hook, not the historical parts.

忙.story: A pounding heart with a fugitive bolting straight through it: nothing in you gets to sit still.
忙.note: 亡 is here for its ボウ sound; the fugitive is a hook, not a claim about meaning.

成.story: The broadaxe swings off a crane arm, stroke after stroke, until the raw beam has become the thing it was always meant to be.

早.story: The sun barely ten fingers above the horizon, and the working day is already underway: early.

曲.story: Seen head-on the graph is a washboard, every rib in it bent — a bend in a line, and the bending of a voice into a tune.

有.story: A left hand reaching up and closing around the moon: whatever you can shut your fingers on, you have.

机.story: One table cut from a single tree, planed flat and shoved against the wall — the desk.

一.story: A single stroke laid flat, with nothing crossing it and nothing stacked above: the count starts at one.

七.story: Cross a fishhook with an upward flick and you have the notch a fisherman scratches for his seventh catch.
七.note: The upward flick and fishhook are only stroke shapes; 七 was originally the picture of cutting (now 切) and got borrowed for the number.

九.story: The stroke curls around and hooks back, stopping a hair short of closing the loop, which leaves it at nine — one shy of ten.

了.story: The curtain rod's last barb catches the cloth, the curtain drops, and the thing is finished.

二.story: Set one on top of one, both flat and both the same length, and you have two.

人.story: Seen from the side, two legs mid-stride and nothing else: every pedestrian out there is just a person walking.

入.story: Two strokes lean together and tuck one edge under the other, leaving a seam you can push through to enter.

八.story: The two strokes fall away from each other, splitting whatever sat between them, and that split is how the old scribes wrote eight.

力.story: A crane arm hauls a load skyward with a slash bracing it from below, which is what power looks like when a body alone isn't enough.

十.story: One stroke runs north-south and another east-west, crossing dead center; count both hands out to the last finger and you are at ten.

万.story: One flat line, a slash, and a crane arm swinging out — three cheap strokes standing in for a number nobody wants to write in full, ten thousand.
万.note: 万 is the squeezed stand-in for 萬, originally a scorpion; none of the three strokes contributes meaning.

三.story: Take two and lay one more underneath: three, the last number you can still draw by simply counting lines.

上.story: A guidepost planted on one flat line of ground, its arm cocked at everything above.

下.story: One line serves as the ceiling and a divining rod dangles from it, pointing at whatever lies below.

与.story: One stroke laid flat inside the open frame and slid across the table toward you — what gets handed over is what you give.
与.note: 与 is the collapsed form of 與, four hands passing something across; the single stroke listed is all that survives of that picture.

久.story: The final stroke drags out into a long, slow tail that never quite lifts off the page, and that drag is the whole point: a long time.

千.story: Slash one mark across the top of ten and the count blows straight past counting: a thousand.

口.story: A plain square hole drawn open and empty, the mouth caught mid-word.

土.story: Ten stakes' worth of digging heaped up above one flat line of ground, and what stands in the pile is earth.

士.story: The same ten over one as in earth, except here the top bar is the broad one: shoulders wider than his stance, the samurai.

夕.story: A beak of moon with a single crumb of light still caught in it, which is all the sky gives you at evening.

大.story: A pedestrian throws out one long crossbar of arms, spanning as wide as a body goes, and that is big.

女.story: Legs folded under, sleeves crossed over: the seated figure the old scribes drew for woman.

子.story: A head too big for the body beneath it, swaddled so tight that only the arms get out — a child.

小.story: A hook down the middle with a fleck shaved off either side, and what survives the shaving is small.

山.story: Three peaks on one baseline with the middle one tallest, the way a mountain looks from a long way off.

川.story: Two banks holding a current that runs hard between them, the river seen from the bridge.

工.story: Two flat faces joined by a shaft: the carpenter's square itself, and picking one up means you are doing craft.

己.story: A cord doubled back on itself twice, forever returning to where it started, which is the self.

才.story: A crowbar is the one tool that turns a weak arm strong, and talent is the leverage you happened to be born holding.
才.note: 'Crowbar' is the shape-handle this app uses for 才; historically the glyph is a shoot pushing up through the ground, so the leverage image is a memory hook, not etymology.

不.story: One line for the sky, roots groping beneath it, and no stem ever breaking through: it did not happen.
不.note: Only the top stroke is listed as a real part — 不 is an old plant picture borrowed purely for its sound as the negative.

中.story: A pole driven clean through a mouth, jutting out top and bottom by equal lengths, dead in the middle.

予.story: The shark fin is still far out at sea and the dangling hook is already baited: everything done beforehand.
予.note: The fin and hook are a pure memory image; 予 is an old drawing of a weaver's shuttle, borrowed here for sound.

五.story: One line caps a zigzag that has doubled back on itself, the tally-keeper's knot for five.

今.story: Under the tent flap an eyebrow lifts, and the instant your eyes meet is now.

介.story: A pedestrian plants himself between a slash on one side and a pole on the other, keeping the two from touching, which is what it is to mediate.

仏.story: A standing person draws his elbow in and shuts the world out: the Buddha.
仏.note: 厶 is the shrunken remnant of 弗 in the older form 佛, which supplied sound only — the standing person carries all the meaning.

元.story: One stroke rests on the flat top of a stool, the head of the whole thing, the origin everything under it stands on.

公.story: Eight pries open a hoarding elbow so that what one person kept gets split and handed round, and that is public.

六.story: A lid over the two splayed legs of eight makes a little hut, a shape borrowed long ago to write six.
六.note: 六 depicts a hut and was taken over purely for its sound; neither lid nor eight has anything to do with the number.

内.story: The pedestrian ducks under the awning and stops there, which puts them inside.

円.story: A squared-off frame with a stroke hanging in it, the flattened descendant of a round coin: one yen.

分.story: Eight strokes of the cleaver hack the hour into slices, and each slice that falls off is a minute.

切.story: Bring the cleaver down on seven and it comes apart right at the crossing: cut.
切.note: 七 is here for the sound セツ, not for seven — fittingly, since 七 was itself the original glyph for cutting.

化.story: A standing person next to a spoon flipped on its head — the same figure inverted, one form turned into another, change.

午.story: A hairpin skewers ten so the long stroke stands bolt upright, the way a shadow shrinks to nothing at noon.

友.story: A left hand comes down to meet a right hand coming up, and the grip that closes is a friend.

双.story: Right hand set beside right hand, identical and matched: a pair.

反.story: A right hand shoves flat against a cliff and strains at rock that will not give, which is how you oppose something.

収.story: The right hand rakes the loose ends in and cinches them with a twist tie, and the bundle it drags home is that season's income.
