収.note: 丩 supplies the sound シュウ and nothing else; the right hand does all the semantic work.

天.story: One line drawn above a big man's outstretched arms, higher than he will ever reach: the sky.

太.story: Big, with a crumb still stuck underneath it, so big and then a bit more — fat.

夫.story: A pedestrian braced by two level bars, one across the shoulders and one pinning his topknot: a grown man, somebody's husband.

少.story: Small, with a slash paring one more sliver off it, leaving only a few.

引.story: Set a pole against the bow and haul the string back until the wood groans: pull.

湯.story: Water droplets left under full sunbeams all afternoon — by the time you step in, the bath is steaming.

湿.story: Water droplets still beaded on the sunlit silk hours after you hung it out — it never quite dries.

満.story: Cram flowers into both halves of the jar, top it off with water droplets, and there is no room left for anything.

無.story: Hairpin pinned, dance plumes fanned wide, one last turn above the cooking fire — and when the dance ends the stage holds nothing at all.
無.note: Originally a picture of a dancer waving plumes; it was borrowed purely for its sound to write the negative, so the parts never really add up to 'nothing'.

然.story: A beak cracking ice out in the yard while the dog hogs the cooking fire — animals doing exactly what animals do, naturally so.
然.note: The character first wrote 'burn' (dog meat over a fire) and was borrowed for the abstract 'thus'; the beak and ice are only what the old meat element broke into.

番.story: Paw prints cross the rice paddy in sets, one animal after another — each set numbered, each beast waiting its turn.

痛.story: Flat on the sickbed with a pipe laid along your spine and something scalding running up it.
痛.note: 甬 is present for its ツウ sound; the pipe is a memory-hook, not part of the meaning.

登.story: Splayed feet step up onto the upturned bean pot to reach the next ledge, and the next, and the next.
登.note: 豆 lends the トウ sound and originally drew a tall ritual stand rather than a bean — take the bean pot as a hook.

着.story: Sheep horns pulled on over your head, one slash of fleece hanging across an eye — dressed at last, and only now do you count as having arrived.
着.note: 着 is a late split-off from 著; its parts are a graphic accident, so this scene is a hook rather than an etymology.

短.story: You measure the long things against an arrow and everything else against a bean — bean-length is short.

税.story: The collector's grin as your grain stalks are loaded onto his cart.
税.note: 兑 supplies the ゼイ sound only — the grin is a hook, not a claim about meaning.

等.story: Bamboo slips at the temple, every one trimmed to the same length and stacked by class.

筋.story: Fibers as straight as split bamboo stand out moon-pale under the skin wherever the muscle pulls.

答.story: Your reply comes back on a bamboo slip cut to fit the question's slip notch for notch.

策.story: A bamboo cane with a thorn lashed to the tip: what you steer a horse with, and what you steer a country with.

結.story: Two threads knotted for good luck at the shrine, and the knot holds all year.

給.story: Each weaver is handed the length of thread that fits her loom — a measured supply, which is all a salary has ever been.

統.story: Fill one fist with every loose thread in the room and pull: scattered strands now governed by a single grip.

絵.story: A meeting of colored threads on the cloth, each crossing the last until a picture stands up out of the weave.

絶.story: Snip the last thread in that color and the whole shade is cut off — no more of it anywhere.
絶.note: The right side is written 色 today but descends from a knife severing threads, so treat 'color' as a hook.

落.story: Flowers dropped onto the Luo River and carried downstream before you can reach them.
落.note: 洛, the Luo river, is here purely for the ラク sound; only the flowers carry meaning.

葉.story: Flowers up top, and hanging off the twig beneath them a thin flat slat — that slat is the leaf.

街.story: Sidewalk down one side, right lane down the other, and a scepter planted at the crossing between them where the market sets out its stalls.

裂.story: Hung in a row, each garment is ripped straight down the seam, collar to hem.

裕.story: A cloak cut so generously you could lose a whole valley in its folds — room to spare, and a purse to match.

覚.story: Sparks go off under the crown of your skull the instant you see it, and that flash is the thing sticking.

証.story: Every word checked off against its own tally mark until nothing is left unaccounted for.

象.story: Read the whole thing as one side view: beak for the trunk, barred box for the ribbed body, trotters for the legs.
象.note: The three pieces are just slices of a single pictograph of an elephant, not meaningful components.

貯.story: Cowrie shells dropped in one at a time and the storage chest lid shut on them.

買.story: Throw the net over what you want, then hand over cowrie shells for the right to keep it.

貸.story: Your cowrie shells go out the door and a paper substitute comes back in — you have lent, not spent.

費.story: A dollar sign stamped across your cowrie shells: already spoken for, already gone.

貼.story: The fortune-teller pockets his cowrie shell and sticks the written fortune to the post where nobody can miss it.
貼.note: Neither part actually says 'paste' — 貝 is money (the word first meant to pledge goods) and 占 carries the sound, so the scene is a hook.

越.story: Run at the line where the sentry's battle axe is planted and clear it in a single stride.

軽.story: The car leaves ruts as fine as the threads of a loom warp, because there is almost nothing to it.

遅.story: A sheep that stops dead in the road and a herder shuffling behind it with all the urgency of a corpse.

遊.story: The banner child skips ahead of the procession down the road, waving the flag purely for the fun of it.

運.story: The army hauls its entire baggage train down the road, and whether the load arrives is a matter of luck.

道.story: A neck cranes to see where the road goes — the path in front of you, and the doctrine you follow down it.

達.story: The lamb slips out onto the road and stands on its first try: it makes it, it arrives.

量.story: At dawn the whole village drags its sacks to the scale to be weighed.

開.story: Lift the bar off the gate and what remains is a bare torii — nothing but sky between the posts.

間.story: Sun shows through the seam where the gate's two leaves don't quite meet.

集.story: One small bird lands in the tree, then forty more, and by dusk the branches are shaking.

順.story: Every head turned the way the river runs, one behind the next, nobody breaking the line.

飯.story: Flip the lid off the pot and white rice steams up at you — the one food a Japanese meal is named after.

飲.story: Mouth cranked open in a yawn while the food goes in in liquid form.

債.story: A standing person you are entitled to point blame at until he pays — that standing claim is the debt.

傾.story: The standing person follows that tilted head over sideways until the whole body goes with it.

働.story: A standing person who will not stop moving — Japan minted its own character just for that.

塗.story: Thin the soil with water droplets until you have a surplus of mud, then smear it across the wall.

奨.story: The general claps a big recruit on the back and shoves him toward the front — encouragement, occasionally with a scholarship attached.

寝.story: Under the roof, the sweeping hand finally sets the broom down and folds onto the bed.

廉.story: Living in a lean-to on two stalks of grain a day — cheap, and honest about being cheap.

微.story: Far up the sidewalk, a tiny peak of a figure you would lose entirely if you blinked.

若.story: Flowers bent hard to starboard by the wind snap straight back up, which only the young stems can do.
若.note: 若 originally depicted a figure combing out long hair; flowers + starboard is a memory hook, not the real origin.

苦.story: Old flowers steeped too long make a tea so bitter that drinking it counts as suffering.
苦.note: 古 is mainly there for the sound (コ→ク); the flower radical carries the 'bitter herb' meaning.

英.story: One flower at the dead center of the bed outshines every other, brilliant enough that Japan borrowed the character to write England.
英.note: 'England' is a sound-borrowing from 英吉利; the composition itself only says 'outstanding flower'.

表.story: The trellis pattern is embroidered onto the hem, on the outside of the garment where the whole street can read it: the surface.

迫.story: A white shape on the road behind you is closer every time you look back, pressing in.
迫.note: 白 supplies only the sound ハク; the road radical carries the meaning.

述.story: Walking the road, you count off every notch on the dotted tree aloud, stating the account point by point.
述.note: 术 contributes the sound (ジュツ), not meaning — hold it as a picture only.

金.story: A pedestrian kneels before the king holding up two horn-shaped nuggets, because nobody brings a king anything but gold.

長.story: One bent nail pins the old chief's hair, and a slash and a right sweep of it still hang past his belt: long.

阻.story: Somebody dragged a bookshelf across the hill path and now nothing gets through.
阻.note: 且 is purely the sound (ソ); the hill is what does the blocking.

雨.story: Under one flat line of cloud the dripping window streams on both panes, because outside it the rain has not let up since morning.

青.story: Moonlight over a trellis turns every leaf on it the same cold shade of blue-green.

乗.story: Read the whole shape as one figure perched in a tree with both feet off the ground, riding whatever he climbed onto.
乗.note: 乗 does not decompose in this system — take the perched shape whole.

亭.story: A lid for a roof, a crown of eaves beneath it, one open mouth of a doorway, one nail of a pillar: a roadside pavilion and nothing more.

便.story: The standing person on night watch sorts your letters while you sleep, which is exactly what convenient means.

係.story: A standing person holds a dangling thread running to every task on the floor: pull any thread and you get the one in charge.

信.story: You never once check the words of that standing person, and that is trust.

則.story: Cowrie shells on the counter and a blade cutting the same notch beside each one, everybody measured identically: the rule.

前.story: Whiskers go under the moon blade first, because they are what sticks out in front.
前.note: the older form was foot + boat ('advance'); whiskers + moon blade is a hook for the modern shape only.

南.story: Ten degrees warmer under the awning that the notched post props up, on the side of the house the sun works all day: south.
南.note: 南 was originally a bronze bell; these parts are a shape hook, not the real etymology.

単.story: Sparks come off one plate of armor with one man inside it and nothing else in the field.
単.note: the original was a forked hunting weapon; sparks-and-armor is a shape hook.

品.story: One mouth up top calls the price down to the pair of chatterboxes below, and all three are haggling over the same crate of goods.

型.story: Clamp soil in a pillory until it quits resisting and keeps the shape you forced on it.

変.story: Armpits soaked and one foot trailing, the man who walks back out of that room is not the one who went in.
変.note: 変 is a simplification of 變 (thread + words + strike); 亦 here is a shape hook, not the original element.

客.story: Feet stop on the welcome mat under a roof that isn't theirs, which makes the person standing there a guest.

室.story: Loose an arrow indoors and it lands in the far corner under the roof, in the boxed-off space you call a room.

専.story: One thumb on one spindle all day, touching nothing else: exclusive attention.

屋.story: The corpse lies flat as a roofline and the arrow lands right beneath it, which is how you know you have reached the shop.

度.story: Under the lean-to a right hand runs down twenty notches cut in the post, calling out each degree as it passes.

建.story: Run the brush up the ramp in one long stroke and leave that line standing upright, the way a building goes up.

待.story: You pace the sidewalk outside the temple until the gate finally opens, which is all waiting ever is.

律.story: A brush has ruled the sidewalk into even paces, and you walk to that measure or you break the law.

後.story: A skein of yarn on the sidewalk snags a trailing foot, and that walker spends the rest of the day behind everyone else.

怒.story: The heart of a slave, held down for years, finally comes up as anger.
怒.note: 奴 mainly supplies the sound (ド); the heart carries the meaning.

思.story: Feelings out of the heart get sorted into the rice paddy's tidy squares upstairs, and that sorting is thinking.
思.note: the top element was originally 囟, the crown of the skull, not a field — the paddy is a hook.

急.story: A snatching hand closes on the heart and the pulse doubles.

持.story: Fingers lock around the temple's donation box and nothing pries them off.
持.note: 寺 is here for the sound (ジ) only; the fingers do all the work.

政.story: A whip stands behind every tally mark to keep the count honest, which is this character's flat opinion of politics.

映.story: The sun catches you dead center and prints your outline on the wall behind you.
映.note: 央 is supplying the sound エイ rather than 'center' as meaning.

春.story: The grain sheaf shoves upward over a sun finally warm enough to pull it.

昨.story: A saw takes the last sun off the end of the calendar, and the day cut away is yesterday.
昨.note: 乍 is purely the sound (サク).

昭.story: Summon the sun indoors and the whole hall goes shining.
昭.note: 召 is chiefly the sound (ショウ) here.

昼.story: Stand a yardstick against the dawn and watch the sun climb it; when it tops the ruler, it is noon.

架.story: Add one more tree crosswise over the uprights and the gap is spanned, ready to carry shelves.

柱.story: One tree trunk carries the whole house, master of every beam that leans on it.
柱.note: 主 is really the sound (チュウ); 'master post' is a hook.

査.story: Every plank cut from the tree comes back off the bookshelf and gets turned over in the light, examined for flaws.
査.note: 査 is a late and obscure form; 且 functions as sound and shape, not meaning.

段.story: Each swing of the war club knocks the ground down one more level, beating out a flight of steps.
段.note: the left half has no keyword in this system — hang the character on the club.

洋.story: Water droplets to the horizon, whitecaps drifting in flocks like sheep: the open ocean, and whatever came from across it.
洋.note: 羊 supplies only the sound (ヨウ).

洗.story: The forerunner hits the water droplets first, so he is the first one washed.
洗.note: 先 is here for the sound (セン) rather than its meaning.

活.story: Water droplets on the tongue and the half-dead man sits up talking, lively again.

海.story: Every water droplet that ever fell is headed to the same address: the sea.

炭.story: Ashes hauled out of the mountain that still catch and burn are charcoal.

点.story: The fortune-teller jabs one finger at a single scorched speck above the cooking fire, and that speck is the point.
点.note: 占 gives the sound (テン) rather than any meaning.

独.story: A wild dog on an empty road with one insect for company still counts as alone.
独.note: the original 獨 had 蜀 as its sound element; 虫 is the leftover of that, not a meaning.

珍.story: Out of the king's whole mane of gems, one catches the light like nothing you will see again.
珍.note: the 王 element here is jade rather than a king, and 㐱 supplies only the sound (チン).

界.story: An armored man is posted at the edge of the rice paddy and lets nobody cross, so that line becomes the boundary of a whole world.

問.story: A mouth planted in the gate, refusing to budge until somebody answers it — a question.

域.story: Soil with a border guard pacing its edge stops being plain dirt and becomes a region.

執.story: Handcuffs clamped on a man curled up in a ball, and nothing he tries pries them open — tenacious.

基.story: The winnowing basket can be picked up and moved anywhere; the packed soil beneath it cannot, and that is the foundation.
基.note: 其 is purely phonetic here — it lends the キ sound, not its meaning. 土 carries the whole sense.

婚.story: Dusk falls and the woman is walked over to her new house — weddings were held after sundown, and marriage still carries the twilight in its spelling.

婦.story: Hand the woman a broom and the old scribes were satisfied: this is the wife of the household.

宿.story: Under one roof, a standing person and ninety-nine more like him — a hundred bodies bedded down for the night is lodging.

密.story: A hushed room with a mountain shoved up against the door: packed dense, and whatever is said inside stays secret.

帳.story: Hang the towel as long as long hair and you have a curtain; rule lines on that cloth and you have a notebook.

常.story: The towel hanging under the smoke vent, greasy and never once taken down — the usual state of things.

張.story: The bow drawn until the string runs out as long as long hair, everything humming — stretched to its limit.

強.story: A bow that can punch an arrow clean through a weevil's armored shell is what strong means.
強.note: 強 originally named a kind of grain weevil; the 'strong' sense is a later loan, so this scene is a memory hook rather than real etymology.

彫.story: Hair-fine grooves scored around the entire circumference of a block until a face stands out of it — carving.

得.story: You are walking the sidewalk when your hand closes on a grabbed shell lying there — money picked up for nothing, pure gain.

悪.story: A heart sealed inside a tomb chamber, airless and slowly going sour — bad.
悪.note: 亜 supplies the sound only; the tomb-chamber image is a memory hook, not the etymology.

情.story: Blue soaks all the way through to the pounding heart — feeling in its undiluted state, and the circumstances that put it there.

掃.story: Fingers clamped around a broom handle, dragging it the length of the boards — sweeping.

授.story: One set of fingers holds it out while the other moves to receive — teaching is simply the giving end of that handoff.

採.story: Fingers dart up into the branches to pluck the one fruit worth having — that one, picked out of all of them.

探.story: Fingers shoved down a dark burrow, patting around blind for whatever is in there — searching.

接.story: Fingers reach out until they close on the handmaid's sleeve — the instant of contact, and everything joined from there on.

推.story: Fingers nudge the small bird off the ledge, and from the way it flies you infer the rest — push first, conclusion after.

救.story: A man in the road begging, and a whip cracking over the horses hauling the wagon out to him — rescue.

教.story: The child rides piggyback and takes a tap of the whip with every line he recites — teaching, old style.

断.story: Rice heaped inside an L-bracket, one axe stroke straight down through the pile — severed, and the matter is decided.

族.story: Whoever comes running when that banner goes up — the one still holding a hairpin, the one still holding an arrow — is family.

望.story: The king stands out under the moon watching the road for the fugitive who never comes back — that long gaze into the distance is hope.

械.story: A tree cut down into levers and catches and set to stand sentry, snapping shut the moment you touch it — a machine.

欲.story: A yawn opened as wide as a valley, and still nothing has filled it — desire.

涙.story: Water droplets that keep returning to the eye no matter how many times you wipe them off — a tear.
涙.note: 戻 is present for its sound; the 'returning' image is a memory hook, not part of the character's meaning.

液.story: Water droplets seeping out through the night, sap and fluid creeping along while nobody is watching.
液.note: 夜 contributes the sound (エキ), not the meaning — the night scene is only a hook.

涼.story: Water droplets sitting in the shade thrown by the capital's tall walls, where the air stays cool all afternoon.
涼.note: 京 is the phonetic; 氵 carries the sense, and the capital's shade is a hook.

添.story: A humbled heart tips a few more water droplets into your cup and then stays at your elbow — appending, accompanying.

清.story: Water droplets running so blue you can count the stones lying under them — pure.

済.story: Water droplets still dripping off everyone as they form up in level rows on the far bank: the crossing is finished, the debt settled.

渉.story: Walking straight into the water droplets instead of going around, thigh-deep and step by step — fording it, and getting involved.

猛.story: The firstborn of the litter is the wild dog that goes for your throat first — fierce.

率.story: Dark thread hung from a pair of horns, eight strands counted against ten knots — that proportion is the rate, and whoever grips the top of the cord leads.
率.note: The composition is opaque and the origin disputed; treat the thread-and-count scene as a pure memory hook.

現.story: The king finally steps out where he can be seen — he appears, and the appearing is the present moment.

球.story: You beg the king for the one flawless round thing in his treasury — a ball.
球.note: 求 is the phonetic (キュウ); the begging is a hook, not part of the meaning.

理.story: The king walks his village lot by lot, straightening every boundary line — the order underneath things, and the work of managing it.

産.story: New life carried out from behind the lectern and presented to the room — a birth, and by extension everything a place produces.

略.story: The whole rice paddy shrunk to the size of a welcome mat — the outline you can take in at a glance, everything else abbreviated away.

盛.story: Keep loading the dish until the pile becomes a mound too tall to carry — heaped, overflowing, prospering.

移.story: Many grain stalks pulled up together and replanted on better ground — the whole crop transfers.

窓.story: A hole knocked in the cave wall to rest your elbow on while your heart wanders off outside — a window.
窓.note: 厶 and 心 are the remains of a phonetic element; only 穴 carries meaning, so the elbow and heart are hooks.

第.story: Bamboo slips lashed to a corded stake in strict sequence, first through last — the mark you set in front of a number.
第.note: 𢎨 supplies only the ダイ sound; the ordering image is a hook.

粗.story: Rice dumped onto the bookshelf still in its husks, unsorted and gritty underfoot — coarse.
粗.note: 且 is purely phonetic (ソ); the bookshelf is a hook.

粘.story: Glutinous rice clings to the fortune-teller's hands and will not shake loose — sticky, and stubborn with it.

累.story: Rice paddies stacked in terraces, each tied to the one above with thread — layer on layer accumulating, plus all the entanglement that brings.

細.story: Thread strung across the ridges of a rice paddy, every strand no thicker than a hairline — thin, and fine enough to show detail.

紹.story: Summon two strangers into the same room and tie a thread between them — that is an introduction.
紹.note: 召 is the phonetic (ショウ); the summoning is a convenient hook rather than the real semantic.

終.story: The thread runs out just as winter closes in — the end of it.

組.story: Loose threads twisted into one braid and set on the bookshelf as a matching set — a group, assembled.
組.note: 且 is phonetic (ソ) here just as in 粗; the bookshelf is a hook.

経.story: Thread running the entire length of the loom warp, end to end without a break — what passes through, and the long business of managing it.

次.story: One yawn passes down the line of people waiting on the ice, and whoever yawns last is next.
次.note: The 冫 here is a flattened 二, not really ice — treat the ice as a shape-hook.

死.story: A spoon scrapes the plate and finds only bones: that is what death leaves behind.
死.note: 匕 is originally a kneeling human figure, not a spoon; the spoon is a pure image-hook here.

毎.story: The barred mother sets her hairpin the same way at the same hour, every single morning of her life.
毎.note: The 'every' sense is a borrowed use; the character originally drew a woman with an elaborate hairpin.

気.story: An X mark scrawled across a cloud of steam — nothing you can catch hold of, yet you feel it the second you walk into a room: that is spirit.
気.note: 㐅 is the postwar squashing of 米 (rice) in 氣; it carries no meaning of its own.

汚.story: Water droplets forced through a bent pipe come out the far end brown, and everything they touch is dirty.
汚.note: 亐 is there only for the sound オ — the bent pipe is a memory-hook, not a meaning.

江.story: Where the coastline turns a hard corner like a carpenter's square, the water droplets stop travelling and sit still: a bay.
江.note: 工 supplies the sound コウ and nothing else; the water is the whole meaning.

池.story: A scorpion crouches on the rim of a hollow full of water droplets and drinks from the pond.
池.note: 也 is purely phonetic (チ) — the scorpion means nothing here beyond being a hook.

百.story: One tally stroke chalked above a white wall, with ninety-nine more to come before the wall is full.
百.note: 白 is here for the sound (ハク → ヒャク), not for whiteness.

考.story: The old man stops walking, puts both hands on his cane, and turns the question over before he answers.
考.note: 丂 mainly carries the sound コウ; the cane is a hook that happens to suit the old man.

耳.story: A narrow upright frame with the outer rim, the inner fold and the hanging lobe drawn straight into it — an ear, seen side-on.

肉.story: A hunk of flesh hanging in the butcher's window, two dark seams of marbling running through the meat.

自.story: A nose drawn straight on, bridge and nostrils; tap your own with a finger in Japan and you have just said "me".

色.story: A beak stabs down at a python, and the snake flares every color it owns.
色.note: The origin of 色 is genuinely disputed; beak-over-python is a shape-hook, not settled etymology.

虫.story: One small insect seen from above: round head, humped body, a single stroke of feelers.

行.story: Sidewalk on the left, right lane on the right, and between them nothing to do but go.
行.note: 行 is really one pictograph of a crossroads; splitting it into 彳 and 亍 is a filing convenience.

西.story: One bar laid over a mouth-wide nest with two legs folded inside — the bird is in for the night, so the sun has gone west.
西.note: 西 is a single pictograph (a nest or basket); the one, legs and mouth are strokes, not real parts.

伺.story: Hat in hand at the boss's door, a standing person waits to be noticed before he asks anything at all.
伺.note: 司 is phonetic (シ); the boss is a hook, though a convenient one for the humble register.

似.story: The standing person drives his plow beside his neighbour's furrow and the two rows come out so alike you cannot tell whose is whose.
似.note: 以 is phonetic (イ) — the plow contributes nothing to the meaning.

位.story: Every standing person has a taped mark on the floor to stand on, and which mark he gets is his rank.

低.story: The standing person is down on the bedrock, flat against it, about as low as a person goes.

住.story: Slippers inside the door and mail on the table: the standing person who is master of this house is the one who actually sleeps here.
住.note: 主 also supplies the sound (ジュウ); the master reading is a helpful hook rather than strict etymology.

体.story: A standing person is bound like a book — covers, spine, the whole physical volume of him — and that volume is the body.
体.note: 体 is the simplified form of 體; 本 here means 'root, substance', and the book is a pure hook.

何.story: The standing person stares up at the green light with no idea what it is telling him to do.
何.note: 可 is purely phonetic (カ); the green light claims no meaning.

余.story: One sapling, and a tent pitched big enough for twenty — all that spare canvas is the surplus.
余.note: 余 stands in for 餘 in the 'surplus' sense; the tent-and-sapling reading is a shape-hook.

作.story: A standing person with a saw, turning a plank into a chair: he makes things.
作.note: 乍 mainly carries the sound サク.

児.story: A skull still soft at the seams, drawn like a fossil, wobbling along on two short legs: a small child.
児.note: 旧 here is a postwar simplification of the infant-skull shape 臼 — nothing to do with 'old'.

冷.story: The orders come down and ice forms on everything — the soup, the room, the handshake.
冷.note: 令 is phonetic (レイ); the orders are a hook, not part of the meaning.

初.story: Before there is a cloak there is a cleaver, and the very first thing that happens to the cloth is a cut.

判.story: Down comes the blade, the case falls in half, and the judge stamps which half was right.

別.story: One slash of the blade opens the mouth-shaped socket and the crane arm lifts the freed half away, separate for good.
別.note: The left half of 別 is a worn-down bone-joint pictograph; mouth, slash and crane arm are strokes rather than genuine parts.

利.story: The blade goes through the grain stalk and every armful that falls is profit.

助.story: Your neighbour's bookshelf is stuck halfway up the stairs, so you put your muscle under one end.
助.note: 且 carries the sound (ジョ); the bookshelf is only a hook for the shape.

努.story: Nothing but the slave's muscle on the oar, stroke after stroke, no talent and no luck involved.
努.note: 奴 is phonetic (ド); the slave is a vivid hook rather than the source of the meaning.

励.story: The whetstone bites, the muscle takes an edge again, and a tired man goes back at it.
励.note: 厉 supplies the sound (レイ); the whetstone is a memory-hook.

労.story: Sparks under the crown of the forge roof and a man's muscle keeping the hammer swinging all afternoon.

医.story: Out comes the arrow, into the open box it goes, and that extraction is where medicine begins.
医.note: 医 is the simplified form of 醫, which also carried 殳 and 酉 (liquor); the box-and-arrow is what survived.

君.story: A gavel in his fist and one mouth the whole hall goes quiet for — the lord, and, softened, the kimi you call a friend.

否.story: The mouth opens and nothing comes out of it but not.

告.story: An ox head over the gate and a mouth beneath it bellowing the news loud enough for the whole street.

困.story: A tree planted inside the city wall, roots against stone on every side, with nowhere left to grow.

囲.story: The city wall goes up in a tight ring around the water well, and now nobody reaches it.
囲.note: 井 replaced 韋 when 圍 was simplified, and it only supplies the sound イ.

図.story: Someone has sketched the city wall on paper and marked icicles and a scythe where the stores are kept.
図.note: 図 is the simplified 圖; the icicles and scythe are leftover strokes, not meaningful parts.

坂.story: Take flat soil and flip one end up: every step across it is now a climb.
坂.note: 反 is there for the sound ハン; the flip is a hook that happens to fit.

声.story: The samurai strikes the hanging chime and what rings back down the hall is so warm and human the crowd hears a voice, not a bell.
声.note: 声 is a clipping of 聲; the samurai on top is really the top of the chime frame.

売.story: The samurai's crown, set out on a stand with legs in the shop window and priced to move.
売.note: 売 is the simplified 賣, which had 貝 (money) underneath; crown and legs are shape-hooks.

対.story: Your writing on one side, my thumb pressed flat against it on the other, the two held up face to face.
対.note: 対 is the simplified 對; 文 is a stand-in stroke group with no meaning of its own.

局.story: Under a corpse-flat roof, a crane arm feeds paperwork through one mouth-shaped service window.
局.note: The composition of 局 is opaque; crane arm and mouth are hooks for the strokes, not established parts.

希.story: Linen woven so thin you can see daylight through every X mark of the weave — scarce stuff.

弟.story: Horns at the top of the corded stake, and each wrap of cord below drops one rank down the family until you reach the younger brother.
弟.note: The character draws cord wound in order around a stake; the 'younger brother' sense comes from that ranking, not from a family scene.

形.story: A torii with fine hair-lines streaming off its posts, the way an artist strokes in an outline.
形.note: 开 supplies the sound ケイ; only 彡, the drawn lines, carries meaning.

役.story: Marched down the sidewalk with a war club at your back until you reach the post they assigned you.

忘.story: Something climbed out of the heart like a fugitive over a wall, and by morning you cannot even say what it was.

応.story: Someone calls for help from under the lean-to, and your heart answers before you have decided to.
応.note: 応 is the simplified 應; the 广 is a leftover of the old upper element, so treat the lean-to as a hook.

快.story: The archer's ring slips the string clean away and the pounding heart goes light with it.
快.note: 夬 is phonetic (カイ); the archer's ring makes no claim on the meaning.

戻.story: Big as he is, he comes back in through the same door he walked out of.
戻.note: The older form had 犬 (dog) under the door; 大 is the postwar reduction.

味.story: The mouth stops talking and rolls a bite of zodiac sheep slowly around, because all the attention has gone to taste.
味.note: 未 is here only for its ミ sound — the sheep contributes no meaning.

呼.story: Mouth to the megaphone, and the whole street learns whose name is being called.
呼.note: 乎 supplies the コ sound; the megaphone is a memory image, not a real meaning.

和.story: One grain stalk between them, and every mouth in the circle gets a share, so nobody fights.
和.note: 禾 is historically the phonetic; the shared-grain scene is a memory hook.

国.story: A jewel sitting inside a ring of city wall: draw that border around what you treasure and you have a country.
国.note: 国 is a simplified form — the jewel stands where an older weapon element sat, so treat it as a hook.

夜.story: Under a lid of black sky, a standing person drags a trailing foot toward home with one crumb of starlight to steer by.
夜.note: These four pieces are the modern silhouette rather than a real composition; the scene is a memory hook.

妹.story: The woman of the house still small enough to ride the zodiac sheep like a pony is the younger sister.
妹.note: 未 is the phonetic (マイ); the sheep means nothing here.

妻.story: Ten pins and one long hairstick fixed above the woman's head — the formal headdress that marks her as a wife.
妻.note: The ten-and-one is just the modern shape of the upper element; take the headdress as an image.

姉.story: Hand the money to the woman old enough to walk to the market alone: that one is your older sister.
姉.note: 市 only lends the シ sound; the market errand is a hook.

始.story: The woman steps up onto the pedestal, the room goes quiet, and whatever this is has officially begun.
始.note: 台 is the phonetic; the pedestal is staging, not meaning.

委.story: The whole grain stalk, heavy head and all, is laid across the woman's arms — the harvest is hers to answer for now.

学.story: Sparks crackle off the top of the crown clamped down over the child's head, which is what a solid hour of study looks like from across the room.
学.note: 学 is simplified from 學 — the 'sparks' are what remains of hands over a schoolhouse.

宗.story: Put an altar under the family roof and you no longer have a house, you have a religion.

定.story: A settled foot planted under a roof ends the wandering, and the matter is decided.

実.story: The grain sheaf stacked under the roof is the year's promise finally made real: fruit you can weigh instead of talk.
実.note: 実 is simplified from 實 (roof over strung money); the sheaf belongs to the modern shape only.

居.story: That corpse has lain in the old house so long it has gone old along with it, so clearly somebody resides here.

届.story: Bent like a corpse under the weight of an oil jar, the carrier hauls it the last block until it reaches the door.

幸.story: The notched post in the soil records how high the flood rose before it stopped, and everyone still dry calls that happiness.

底.story: Sweep the lean-to out and the broom hits bedrock: the bottom, with nothing underneath it.

店.story: A fortune-teller sets up under a roadside lean-to, and by evening the pitch has become a shop.
店.note: 占 gives the テン sound only; the fortune-teller is a hook.

府.story: Under the official lean-to, every crate wears a sticker naming its district — the government seat a prefecture is run from.
府.note: 付 is the phonetic (フ); the sticker is an image, not the sense.

彼.story: Not this man on the sidewalk — the one in the pelt further along, him, over there.
彼.note: 皮 carries only the ヒ sound; the pelt is a costume for memory.

念.story: The heart is carrying a stone that landed on it just now and shows no sign of rolling off — call that a thought.

性.story: The pounding heart you were issued at the start of life and cannot exchange: your nature.

房.story: Off the main hall, a door with its own banner hanging above it opens into a small side room.
房.note: 方 is the phonetic (ボウ); the banner merely marks the doorway for you.

所.story: The axe lives leaning against the door, and that corner is its place — everyone in the house knows it.

承.story: Take the relay baton without breaking stride: you have heard the instruction and it is yours to carry now.

押.story: Fingers flat against a slab of armor, whole body leaning in — push.

担.story: At dawn the fingers close on the carrying pole and the whole load goes up onto one shoulder.
担.note: 旦 lends the タン sound; dawn is scenery, not meaning.

招.story: Words alone only summon someone; add fingers curling in toward your chest and they actually accept the invitation.

拝.story: Fingers pressed flat, back bent in one long line, the rake let fall in the dirt: the man is worshipping.
拝.note: 拝 comes from 拜, a picture of two bowing hands; the rake is a memory prop.

放.story: One crack of the whip and the banner is let go, snapping away downwind.
放.note: 方 is the phonetic (ホウ) and adds nothing to the meaning; the banner is only an image.

昇.story: The sun clears the rim of the measuring cup and keeps climbing.
昇.note: 升 supplies the ショウ sound; the cup is just a horizon to rise over.

明.story: Sun and moon in the sky at the same hour, and suddenly there is nowhere left to hide.

昔.story: Hurdle stacked on hurdle on top of the sun — that many days piled up between then and now.
昔.note: 龷 is only the modern shape of the upper element; the hurdles are a counting image.

東.story: The whole shape is a sack corded top and bottom, slung on a shoulder and carried toward the first light.
東.note: 東 is taken whole — it depicts a tied bundle, and the popular 'sun behind a tree' reading is folk etymology.

板.story: Split the tree, flip the slab, and the flat face you land on is a board.

林.story: Two trees standing close enough to shade each other and nothing more: a grove.

枚.story: Take the whip to the tree until it splits into thin flat pieces, then count them off one at a time.

枠.story: Ninety identical strips of tree, mitred and pinned, box the picture in and tell it where to stop.
枠.note: 枠 is a Japanese-coined character; 卆 contributes no meaning — the ninety is a pure hook.

歩.story: One footprint, then a few more, and you have invented walking.

毒.story: Both arms out, the barred mother blocks the trellis, because every glossy leaf climbing it is poison.

治.story: Channel the water droplets neatly around the pedestal and the flood answers to you — the same word covers running a province and curing a body.
治.note: 台 is the phonetic; the pedestal is an image only.

泊.story: The hull halts where the water droplets break white against it, and the crew sleeps aboard.
泊.note: 白 gives the ハク sound; the whiteness is scenery, not sense.

法.story: Water droplets exit downhill by the same route every time, asking nobody's permission, and that fixed course is what law means.

注.story: The master tips the pot so the water droplets land exactly where he means them to, which is why the word also carries 'attention'.

泳.story: Give the swimmer his water droplets at last and he does the one thing he was ever drawn for.

炉.story: Fire kept behind a little door you can swing open when the room turns cold.
炉.note: 炉 is simplified from 爐; 戸 stands in for the old phonetic and carries no meaning.

物.story: Every cow in the herd is tagged with its own streamers so you can tell one from the next, and that separating-out is what makes a thing a thing.

画.story: One ruled stroke laid across the mouth of the pit, an oil jar of ink at your elbow, and the picture goes down stroke by countable stroke.
画.note: These parts are the modern silhouette (older forms show a brush over a field); the scene is a hook.

的.story: A white disc no bigger than a teacup at the far end of the range, with every arrow in the quiver pointed at it.
的.note: 勺 is the phonetic (テキ); the teacup only gives you the size.

直.story: Ten times the eye runs down the beam past an L-bracket, and anything off true gets pushed straight.

知.story: The answer leaves the mouth like an arrow: straight out, no wobble, no pause to think.

空.story: Work a cave over with a carpenter's square until nothing at all is left inside, and what you are left holding is sky.

者.story: An old man parked in the sun all afternoon, no name given, just the person who does that.
者.note: 者's parts are a late reshaping of an opaque original; the old-man-in-the-sun is a memory image.

育.story: The newborn arrives head-downward, and under the same moon, year after year, somebody raises it.
育.note: The 月 here is really the flesh radical, not the moon; the moon is the app's stand-in image.
